The pin needs a surface behind the target and holds a single target at a time; a strong, heavy or well-braced opponent can work free, and you must keep the target in sight and your attention on it. It is restraint, not harm: applied carelessly it bruises and breaks fingers, and applied at the throat or chest it is a lethal weapon and treated as one.

[innate biological action]

Fault Split.name: Fault Split
Fault Split.description:
Open a controlled break through a mass of stone, masonry or compacted debris along a line you choose, splitting it into pieces that can be moved or letting a wall section drop where you want it.

The split follows real weaknesses; sound, homogeneous material resists, and the pieces fall as gravity dictates, not by your choice. It is demolition: loud, slow to set up and dangerous to everyone near the line, and used on an occupied or load-bearing element it brings down more than intended. Living bodies are not a valid target.

[innate biological action]

Rescue Shear.name: Rescue Shear
Rescue Shear.description:
Separate a bonded or jammed thing from the thing beside it without harming either: a trapped limb from twisted wreckage, a fused component from a live device, a collapsed beam from the person beneath it.

The cut is fine and slow and requires clear sight and a steady hand; movement, panic or poor light make it a hazard rather than a tool. It is precision, not power: it will not cut a heavy mass or hold anything up, and the freed person still needs a medic. Working a long extraction leaves your own hands numb and shaking.

[innate biological action]

Iron Sense.name: Iron Sense
Iron Sense.description:
Feel the presence and rough position of responsive metal nearby through cover: a hidden blade, buried fittings, a dropped tool in dark water, the frame behind a panel.

The sense is coarse, a pull rather than a picture; it distinguishes near from far and heavy from light, not shape or kind, and it fades quickly through thick stone or many layers. It cannot identify what a piece is, read a device or reach through a shielded case, and searching a wide area is a long, patient job.

[innate biological action]

Plate Interpose.name: Plate Interpose
Plate Interpose.description:
Shift a worn or carried metal plate, a buckler, a pauldron, a breastplate section, to meet an incoming blow without moving your hands or breaking stride.

Only metal already fitted to you or in your grasp answers; it moves as far as its straps and your own body allow, and a blow heavy enough to crush the plate is not stopped by moving it. It does not catch projectiles you have not seen, does not raise a full guard and cannot be held ready indefinitely.

[innate biological action]

Cold Bond.name: Cold Bond
Cold Bond.description:
Fuse a pair of compatible metal pieces into a single continuous piece along a seam, a real join that lasts: closing a split casing, mending a broken frame, fixing a plate to a hull.

The pieces must be in contact and of compatible alloy; dissimilar metals, contaminated surfaces or a seam under load yield a weak join that fails later. This is joining, not fabrication: it makes no new parts, restores no working mechanism and does nothing to non-ferrous material. A long seam is exhausting and leaves your hands cramped.

[innate biological action]

Pulled Arsenal.name: Pulled Arsenal
Pulled Arsenal.description:
Wrench ferrous weapons, tools and loose equipment out of several hands and holsters at once across an area, gathering them to a point you choose.

Only responsive metal in the open answers; holstered or sheathed items come free slower than drawn ones, a hand that grips hard keeps its blade, and an implant, a sealed device or a non-ferrous weapon is untouched. The gathered mass arrives fast and dangerously and lands where you send it, not neatly. Doing this in a crowd takes full attention, and the recoil of a large pull is felt as strain in your own arms and back.

[innate biological action]

Wire Trace.name: Wire Trace
Wire Trace.description:
Follow a live current path by feel along its length: wiring behind a wall, a cable through wreckage, the feed to a sealed device.

The trace needs current actually flowing; dead or dormant lines give nothing, and lines run close together blur. It tells you where power runs, not what it powers or what it carries; it does not read data, identify a device or reveal anything behind shielding. Following a long run is slow, and repeated tracing leaves a headache and tingling hands.

[innate biological action]

Sensor Shadow.name: Sensor Shadow
Sensor Shadow.description:
Bend the scanning fields around your own body so that electromagnetic sensors, proximity detectors and field-based alarms read nothing where you stand.

The shadow covers you and what you carry; it does not hide anyone else, defeat a watching eye or a camera, silence noise, or stop a sensor that works by another medium. Moving quickly through a dense array lets edges of you show, and the effort of holding it while doing anything else is a steady drain.

[innate biological action]

Borrowed Flow.name: Borrowed Flow
Borrowed Flow.description:
Divert a flow of ambient or redirected electrical energy into a dead circuit, a stalled lift, a locked door, a dark console, a fallen companion's medical unit, and hold it running for a short while.

Nothing is generated; there must be a live source nearby, and the borrowed flow runs only while you hold the path and never stronger than the source allows. The device must still be intact, the wrong rate burns it out, and holding a heavy load leaves you shaking, with burns along the path it took through you.

[innate biological action]

Live Circuit Map.name: Live Circuit Map
Live Circuit Map.description:
Perceive every active field in a whole structure at once, a building, a ship, a compound, laying out its live circuits, running devices, hidden sensors and power sources as a single felt map.

The map shows what is live and where, not what it does, what it carries or what it thinks; dormant systems, shielded rooms and mechanical locks do not appear on it. Reading a large, busy structure is disorienting and can be held only for a short stretch before headache, nosebleed and a temporary loss of the sense itself set in.

[innate biological action]

Held Ballast.name: Held Ballast
Held Ballast.description:
Shift personal density into the limb or shoulder bearing a load, so a braced door, a held line or a pinned object stays where the user is holding it.

Grown from Rooted Stance: the anchoring now goes into what the user is holding rather than only the user's own footing. It works only through the user's own body and only while contact is kept; letting go releases everything at once. The supporting ground still carries the combined weight, and a load that would crush an ordinary grip still crushes this one. It cannot make an object heavier for anyone else, and it does not hold against forces that lift the user off the surface.

[innate biological action]

Anchored Chain.name: Anchored Chain
Anchored Chain.description:
Extend the anchoring through direct contact to the people holding onto the user, so a linked line of bodies resists wind, current, crowd surge or a hard pull as if each of them were rooted.

The expression passes along grip: whoever is touching the user, and whoever is touching them in turn, shares the resistance while the chain holds. Range is the length of the linked line and no further, and a broken grip drops that person and everyone beyond them at once. The user still needs supporting ground and cannot anchor a chain that is airborne or in open water. Holding a line under a real surge is exhausting, and the strain lands on the user first.

[innate biological action]

Load Shift.name: Load Shift
Load Shift.description:
Move the balance point of a large object under contact by redistributing density within it, tipping a leaning slab back over its support or settling a nose-light vehicle.

Earlier anchoring made things heavy or light as a whole; this places the weight precisely inside a single object, with enough finesse to steady it rather than drop it. Mass is moved, not created: total weight is unchanged and something must still bear it. Contact is required throughout and the effect ends when the hand leaves. Objects in free fall, liquids and living bodies cannot be rebalanced, and a member that is failing will still fail.

[innate biological action]

Ground Keel.name: Ground Keel
Ground Keel.description:
Become the fixed point for a whole platform, moored craft, gantry or floor section, anchoring it against sliding, tipping or lift by holding its density to the user's own rooted body.

The growth is duration and scale, not force: the anchoring is held steadily over minutes, through the user's own movement across the structure and through pain, without the hard release that disorients below. The user must stand on solid ground or a surface bearing onto it; nothing is kept from falling out of the air, and what the ground cannot support cannot be saved. Sustaining it drains stamina continuously; dropping it early lets everything move at once.

[innate biological action]

Soft Landing.name: Soft Landing
Soft Landing.description:
Bleed momentum from the user's own body at the moment of landing, so a drop, a hard flight arrival or a stumble ends with far less force through the legs and spine.

Gentle Catch worked on a caught object; this applies the same softening to the user's own mass. It shortens a fall's consequence, not its height: a long drop still hurts, and one taken without warning still lands badly. It softens nothing else in the scene, does not slow a fall in the air and cannot be spent on someone else. Timing matters; the working must be set before contact, and a landing on a surface that gives way still gives way.

[innate biological action]

Crowd Damping.name: Crowd Damping
Crowd Damping.description:
Soften the forward momentum of many people at once in a crush, a stampede or a panicked corridor, taking the lethal force out of the press without stopping anyone.

Reach grows from one moving body to a dense crowd within the practised range, at the cost of depth: each person is slowed only a little, enough to prevent crushing against a wall or a fallen body, not to freeze the crowd. It must be held continuously while the press lasts and fails the moment attention breaks. The energy bled from the crowd still has to go somewhere, and the user feels it as strain. It cannot pick out one person in the crowd for more than the rest.

[innate biological action]

Selective Bleed.name: Selective Bleed
Selective Bleed.description:
Drain momentum from a single chosen moving thing among many, slowing the thrown blade without touching the ally's arm beside it, or stopping one falling stone while the rest of the slide runs on.

Precision is the growth here: the working discriminates by choice rather than by area, and can be applied inside a chaotic exchange where earlier softening would slow friend and foe alike. It holds for one subject at a time, within reach of the expression, and switching subjects costs a fresh effort. It cannot stop anything instantly, and something fast enough still arrives. Concentration under fire is real, and a wrong choice softens the wrong thing.

[innate biological action]

Crash Envelope.name: Crash Envelope
Crash Envelope.description:
Wrap a whole vehicle, a falling gantry or a collapsing room and everyone inside it in softening through the entire impact sequence, from the first jolt to the last settling of debris.

Inertial Command stopped one vehicle or cushioned one collapse; this holds softening across every moving piece for the seconds the event lasts, while the user is moving, hurt or inside the wreck. It lessens each impact within the envelope; it does not prevent the crash, hold the structure up or protect against fire, cutting edges or drowning. The bled momentum passes into the ground and the user's body, and a full envelope can put the user down beside those it saved.

[innate biological action]

Taken Blow.name: Taken Blow
Taken Blow.description:
Step into the path of a blow aimed at someone within arm's reach and absorb it into the user's own expression instead.

Absorbing Brace protected only the user's own stance; this spends the same absorption on another person's behalf. The user must physically be able to reach the line of the blow before it lands, and takes the strain of the hit in their own body. One blow at a time; a second strike while the first is being absorbed lands normally. It does not cover a blow the user cannot see coming, and it does not shield anyone from anything that is not a physical impact.

[innate biological action]

Ground Sink.name: Ground Sink
Ground Sink.description:
Send an absorbed impact down through the stance into the floor or the ground, dissipating it downward instead of outward, so a heavy hit can be taken in a crowded room without throwing bystanders.

Dispersal Wave pushed force out; this chooses the direction and sends it where no one is standing. It needs solid footing that connects to a mass able to take the force, and on a thin floor, a ledge or a deck it can damage what it drains into. The user still carries the strain of the absorption itself, and a force larger than the stance can channel breaks the footing rather than draining away. It does not store anything for later.

[innate biological action]

Rolling Intake.name: Rolling Intake
Rolling Intake.description:
Take a run of impacts in succession, a barrage, a fall of rubble or a sustained pounding, by spreading the absorption across the whole body and metering it out continuously rather than swallowing each hit whole.

Earlier tiers warned that absorption in succession was dangerous; this makes it survivable through control, not immunity. Each impact still lands and tires the body, but the accumulated force is bled off as it arrives instead of building to a dangerous hold. The user cannot move quickly while doing it and covers only the directions the stance faces. A single structural-scale impact still needs the full stance and full attention.

[innate biological action]

Shelter Stance.name: Shelter Stance
Shelter Stance.description:
Become the absorbing element for a huddled group or a small hull, taking a structural-grade impact on behalf of everyone in contact with the user and bleeding it into the ground beneath.

Scale grows from one body to everyone the user can touch, and the working holds through the user's own injury. The user must be between the group and the force, in contact with them, and standing on something that can take what is drained into it. It absorbs impact only, not heat, cutting force or suffocation, and cannot hold up a structure already coming down. What cannot be dissipated stays in the user's body; a full blast taken for others can drop them.

[innate biological action]

Loaded Pry.name: Loaded Pry
Loaded Pry.description:
Reinforce a shove, a lift or a pry and release the stored effort through a tool or directly into a stuck object, freeing a jammed hatch, shifting a fallen beam or breaking a seized fitting loose.

Reinforced Contact released through a strike; this tier releases through a tool or a braced push, for work rather than combat. The release is a single surge at the moment of effort, not a sustained increase in strength, and what the user could not begin to move with ordinary effort still does not move. A tool that cannot take the load breaks. Recovery is real: a hard release leaves the arms shaking and the next one is weaker.

[innate biological action]

Thrown Surge.name: Thrown Surge
Thrown Surge.description:
Load stored kinetic energy into an object the user throws or launches, so the release happens where the object lands rather than at the user's hand.

The medium of release changes: a thrown stone, a dropped weight or a cast line carries the charge and gives it up on impact. The charge decays with distance and time in the air, so the release is strongest close and weakens over a long throw. The object must be thrown by the user's own body; nothing fired from a machine carries it. Aim is ordinary aim, and a miss spends the charge on whatever was hit. Only one object holds a charge at a time.

[innate biological action]

Banked Charge.name: Banked Charge
Banked Charge.description:
Hold a stored kinetic charge steady across time and movement, through a run, a climb or a flight, and choose the moment of release later instead of at the instant of loading.

Kinetic Burst dissipated if mistimed; this tier keeps the charge banked in the body without leakage while the user moves, and lets the release be placed with precision when the opening arrives. The charge is still the user's own stored effort and is not free: carrying it costs stamina the whole time, and being struck hard while banked can release it uncontrolled. It cannot be stored across a night's sleep, and only one charge can be banked at once.

[innate biological action]

Split Discharge.name: Split Discharge
Split Discharge.description:
Release a stored cascade through several contact points at once, both hands, a foot and a hand, or a blow and an infusion into an ally in the same instant, dividing the energy deliberately between them.

Where Kinetic Cascade layered everything into one release, this divides it, and each portion is smaller than the whole. The user must be in contact with every target of the release at the moment it happens; nothing goes to a target out of reach. The division is chosen in advance, and under pressure a split can go uneven. The body is still the capacitor and pays for the whole of what was stored, whichever way it left.

[innate biological action]

Glance Plane.name: Glance Plane
Glance Plane.description:
Set the barrier at an angle across an approach so incoming force glances off it and away instead of being borne head-on.

Guard Face took impacts squarely; this tier turns them. Deflection needs less of the user than absorption, but the angle must be set before the impact and chosen for that impact; a blow from an unexpected line meets no plane. What is deflected goes somewhere real and can strike a wall, a companion or the user's own leg. The plane covers a single approach at once and cannot be wrapped around the body.

[innate biological action]

Doorway Screen.name: Doorway Screen
Doorway Screen.description:
Leave a barrier standing across a doorway, a gap or a corridor mouth while the user steps back a few paces from it, holding it in place by attention rather than by standing behind it.

The barrier is no longer fixed to the user's body: it can cover others passing through, or hold an opening the user has left. It stays only within the practised range and only while the user keeps attention on it; a turn to fight or a hard shove of pain lets it drop. It holds one opening at a time, cannot be walked through by allies without the user lowering it, and takes the full force of whatever hits it into the user's stamina as if they were standing there.

[innate biological action]

Ringed Cover.name: Ringed Cover
Ringed Cover.description:
Raise a barrier around a small group rather than around the user alone, covering several people huddled or standing together against impact from any side.

Barrier Shell covered one body; this covers a cluster, at the cost of thickness, since the same expression is spread over a larger surface. Everyone covered must stay within arm's reach of one another and near the user, and someone stepping out steps out of the cover. Concentration must be held continuously and gaps open if attention splits, exactly as with the shell. It does not identify friend from foe; anyone inside the ring is covered, anyone outside is not.

[innate biological action]

Moving Bulwark.name: Moving Bulwark
Moving Bulwark.description:
Hold a barrier over a moving group, a vehicle or a flight in formation while it travels at speed, keeping the cover intact through sustained fire, through turns and through the user's own injury.

Movement broke every earlier barrier; this keeps one whole while what it covers moves fast and the user moves with it. The cover is still limited to the practised range around the user and thins as it spreads over a larger body. It is not immunity: heavy, repeated impact wears it down, and the strain of holding it under fire builds until the user fails. Nothing passes through in either direction while it stands, including the group's own return fire.

[innate biological action]

Skid Stop.name: Skid Stop
Skid Stop.description:
Arrest the user's own slide, skid or slip on a surface, halting a fall down a slope, a slide across ice or a stumble on a slick deck.

Arrest Touch worked on a chosen movement under contact; this applies the lock to the user's own body against the ground beneath it. It stops sliding, not falling through air, and needs a surface to lock against. The stop is sudden and can wrench a joint at speed. It does not help a companion sliding beside the user, does not fix the user in place afterward and cannot hold against a pull from something else once the slide is stopped.

[innate biological action]

Fixed Grip.name: Fixed Grip
Fixed Grip.description:
Lock the vector of a held tool, weapon or object so it cannot be twisted out of the hand, dragged away or shifted off its line while the user holds it.

Directional Lock arrested another body's movement; this holds the movement of what the user carries. A locked grip resists disarming, a snatched line and a bucking tool, and can hold a spinning or swinging part still long enough to work on it. The lock holds only while the user's hand is on the object and concentration is kept; the object itself is not strengthened, and a force that would break it still breaks it. It does not lock the user's arm in place.

[innate biological action]

Walking Hold.name: Walking Hold
Walking Hold.description:
Hold a lock on a single movement vector without maintaining contact, keeping a beam from falling or a rolling load from moving while the user walks out from under it or around it.

Every earlier lock ended when contact broke; this one survives it, within the practised range, for as long as the user can keep attention on the held vector while moving. One vector on one subject; a second demand drops the first. The held object is not supported, only stopped along that line, and it can still move on any line the lock does not cover. Distance and distraction both wear the hold down, and it fails outright if the user is struck or falls.

[innate biological action]

Ordered Release.name: Ordered Release
Ordered Release.description:
Hold several separate vectors on separate subjects at once, a falling load, a rolling vehicle, a charging body, each on its own line, and release them one at a time in a chosen order.

Vector Sovereignty froze an area; this manages it, keeping distinct locks under distinct control and letting them go deliberately. The number of holds is limited by concentration, not by the scene, and each one added makes the others harder to keep. Everything held still has its force waiting behind the lock, and a release out of order sends it exactly where it was going. Multi-locking exhausts the user rapidly and cannot be kept up while fighting.

[innate biological action]

Passing Lane.name: Passing Lane
Passing Lane.description:
Perceive the line a thrown object, a cast cable or a companion could take through a visible arrangement, rather than only the user's own path.

Clear Line found the user's route; this finds one for something or someone else, and gives the user a concrete picture of the gap it must pass through. It perceives the line only; hitting it still depends on the throw, the cable or the companion's own ability. Only visible arrangements are read, and only for a single line at a time. It cannot see what will move into the gap after the object is released.

[innate biological action]

Moving Gap.name: Moving Gap
Moving Gap.description:
Perceive routes through moving obstacles, crowds, traffic or drifting debris, sensing where a gap is opening and how long it will stay open.

Earlier perception mapped fixed structure; this tier reads the arrangement as it changes and anticipates the next opening from present movement. It is not foresight: an obstacle that changes direction without warning closes a gap the user was counting on, and anything the user cannot sense is not in the picture. It holds a picture for the user's own movement or one companion's, not a formation, and its reach is the practised range. Reading a fast crowd for long is tiring.

[innate biological action]

Called Path.name: Called Path
Called Path.description:
Convey a perceived route to others accurately enough for a group to follow it in real time, calling turns, gaps and footing as the user moves ahead or watches from a vantage.

The perception is Route Mastery's; what grows is the ability to hand it on. The user holds a moving picture of several companions' positions within the mapped space and gives each the next step before they need it, on foot or in flight. It works only with people who can hear or see the user and follow the call; it moves no one, and a companion who cannot make the step still cannot. The map is limited to what the expression senses, so sealed areas stay blank.

[innate biological action]

Airspace Weave.name: Airspace Weave
Airspace Weave.description:
Perceive routes through a district's airspace in three dimensions at flight speed, tracking many moving craft and flyers at once and holding a continuous picture of the open lines between them.

Reach grows to the volume of a district and the subjects tracked to everything moving in it that the expression can sense, sustained through the user's own fast flight and through injury. It is perception, not control: nothing in the sky moves because the user sees it, and a craft turning without warning can close a line. Reading a crowded sky for long is draining and the picture narrows as the user tires; it does not see through weather or structure.

[innate biological action]

Footfall Count.name: Footfall Count
Footfall Count.description:
Through a floor, a wall or a shared support, count the people moving in an adjoining space and place roughly where each is, from their footfalls alone.

Surface Listen gave a meaningful signal; this tier resolves it into a count and a placement. It tells how many and where, not who, not what they carry and not what they intend. Heavy machinery, a crowd or an insulating layer between the user and the space blurs the count, and a person standing still gives nothing. The user must stay in contact with the connected surface, and the picture is only as current as the last step taken.

[innate biological action]

Ground Reach.name: Ground Reach
Ground Reach.description:
Extend vibration sensing through the ground itself, feeling approaching vehicles, digging, foot traffic or the onset of collapse across a street, a yard or a field.

Reach grows from a single structure to the ground it stands on and what that ground connects to. The signal is coarser at distance: a vehicle is recognisable long before it is identifiable, and what is felt is movement and direction, not detail. Soft earth, running water or a deliberately isolated foundation cut the reach short. The user must be in solid contact with the ground and still enough to read it; walking spoils the picture.

[innate biological action]

Break Warning.name: Break Warning
Break Warning.description:
Hold continuous vibration sensing on a loaded structure while working on or moving through it, feeling the onset of a failure in time to call it before the break.

Seismic Authority read a structure at rest; this reads it under changing load, with the user's own weight and movement on it, and gives a warning with enough lead to act on. The warning is a felt change, not a diagnosis, and it gives moments, not minutes. It is limited to the structure the user is touching and to failures that announce themselves through vibration; a clean shear with no precursor gives no warning. Holding the sensing while also working splits attention and tires quickly.

[innate biological action]

Span Listening.name: Span Listening
Span Listening.description:
Read a whole connected structural network, a bridge span, a tower cluster or a rail line, through vibration, holding continuous awareness of movement, load and fault across all of it while machines run.

Scale grows to everything the user's contact point is structurally connected to, and reliability grows to reading through the ordinary noise of a working structure rather than needing quiet. It cannot cross a true break or an isolating joint, and the farthest parts of the network are read only coarsely. It is awareness, not intervention, and does not identify people or read intent. Sustaining it is exhausting and narrows as the user tires.

[innate biological action]

Live Check.name: Live Check
Live Check.description:
Tell by contact whether a compatible device is holding charge, armed, running on standby or truly dead, before touching anything that could trigger it.

State Glimpse read one supported operational state; this tier answers a single practical question reliably: is it live. It does not say what the device will do when triggered, what it stores or who armed it, and it gives nothing on a machine the expression is not compatible with. Shielded, sealed or deliberately masked systems can read as dead. Contact or close proximity is required, and the answer is for that moment only.

[innate biological action]

Fault Trace.name: Fault Trace
Fault Trace.description:
Follow a fault through a linked system to its origin, sensing which component in a chain of connected machines is actually failing and which are only reacting to it.

System Diagnosis read one machine in full; this tier reads across several connected ones and separates cause from symptom. The trace runs along physical or electrical connection the user can reach or stay close to, and stops at any break the expression cannot cross. It names the failing element, not the repair, and does not restore anything. Systems built to hide faults from each other can mislead it, and a large network takes time and steady attention to walk.

[innate biological action]

Tamper Signature.name: Tamper Signature
Tamper Signature.description:
Distinguish deliberate tampering from wear, damage and honest fault with precision, and describe the kind of interference: cut, bridged, reprogrammed, replaced or overridden.

The awareness deepens into the character of a fault rather than only its presence. The user can say with confidence that a machine was interfered with and roughly how, which is what an inspection or a dispute needs. It does not say who did it, when beyond rough recency, or what the tampering was meant to achieve. Careful work by someone who knows the expression exists can pass as wear. This remains awareness, not control; nothing is restored or overridden by reading it.

[innate biological action]

Fleet Watch.name: Fleet Watch
Fleet Watch.description:
Hold continuous awareness of many machines at once over a working shift, a hangar's craft, a ship's systems or a drone swarm, noticing each change of state as it happens while doing other work.

Machine Authority swept every machine in range once; this keeps the sweep running, so a state change anywhere in the set surfaces to the user as it occurs. Reliability under load is the growth: the watch survives the user's own work, movement and fatigue, though it narrows as the user tires. Range is still the expression's reach, compatibility still limits what is seen, and a shielded system can still hide. It is diagnostic only; nothing is commanded.

[innate biological action]

Worn Control.name: Worn Control
Worn Control.description:
Draw a usable response from a worn, sticking or half-dead control, a lever with a dead zone, a failing touch panel or a switch that only catches on repeated tries, by adapting to the fault through touch.

Responsive Touch smoothed a working interface; this tier makes a damaged one work for the user. The control must still function at some level; a truly dead input gives nothing, and the fault is not repaired, only compensated for. The compensation is personal and does not transfer to anyone else using the same control. Complex or safety-critical controls under load remain slower and riskier than a sound interface.

[innate biological action]

Blind Operation.name: Blind Operation
Blind Operation.description:
Operate a physical interface the user has handled before without sight, in darkness, smoke or by reaching into a housing, relying on touch alone.

The senses used change: Interface Calibration learned by touch and sight together, and this tier holds a full picture of a known interface through the hands alone. It applies to interfaces already learned, not to unfamiliar ones, and precision falls on controls that relied on visual readouts. Feedback the interface gives only by light or screen is lost. Under vibration or with gloves the picture degrades, and a rearranged control set is as unfamiliar as a new one.

[innate biological action]

Divided Hands.name: Divided Hands
Divided Hands.description:
Operate an interface with each hand independently at once, or pass a task from one hand to the other without losing place, keeping full tactile adaptation on both under vibration or acceleration.

The growth is in how many controls can be held in adaptation at once and in composure under motion. Separate interfaces, or separate regions of a complex one, can be worked without one degrading the other, at a pace useful in a craft under load. Each hand operates only what it can physically reach, and adaptation does not extend to controls neither hand is on. It adds no machine function, bypasses no security and makes no difficult sequence simple.

[innate biological action]

Foreign Console.name: Foreign Console
Foreign Console.description:
Adapt to an interface built for another species' body or a different technology entirely, an Olyth pressure surface, a Zencadian implant-linked panel or salvaged offworld hardware.

Interface Mastery handled interfaces of a kind the user knew; this meets one built on assumptions the user's body does not share and finds a working match through touch. It takes time on first contact and stays slower than a native operator; controls that need an implant, a limb the user lacks or a biometric the user cannot supply stay closed. Security is not bypassed and a locked function stays locked. Sustained foreign work is tiring and errors under fatigue are real.

[innate biological action]

Batch Match.name: Batch Match
Batch Match.description:
Tell by handling a pair of samples whether they come from the same source, batch or piece, matching a shard to a vessel, a cut length to its coil or a fragment of cloth to a garment.

Material Impression sensed one authenticity-related property; this tier compares, and gives a confident same-or-different for a pair. It says whether they match, not where either came from, who made them or which one is genuine. Materials that are naturally uniform across many batches can read as matching when they are not, and heavy contamination on either sample spoils the comparison. Contact with both samples is required, and the reading covers one pair at a time.

[innate biological action]

Contact Residue.name: Contact Residue
Contact Residue.description:
Read what a material has recently been in contact with, a hand, a container, a chemical, a surface, from the trace it left, well enough to name the class of thing if not the individual.

Provenance Read traced handling history over a long timeline; this tier resolves the most recent contacts in finer detail. It names kinds, not people: skin rather than a person, an oil rather than a brand, a metal container rather than which one. Older contacts are overwritten by newer ones, and a surface washed or worn since gives little. Contact is required, and it cannot say what the contact meant or intended. It supports an investigation; it does not close one.

[innate biological action]

Altered Layers.name: Altered Layers
Altered Layers.description:
Distinguish deliberate alteration from genuine age and wear, separating forgery, artificial aging, replaced parts and later repair from the original state, in the order they were applied.

The reading deepens into sequence: not only that an object was altered but which changes came first and which were made to look older than they are, as an appraisal or a dispute needs. It cannot name the forger, date a layer beyond rough order and recency, or read an object newly assembled from genuinely old material as anything but old parts. Skilled alteration made with knowledge of this expression can be missed. Contact is required and a full reading takes time.

[innate biological action]

Cargo Sweep.name: Cargo Sweep
Cargo Sweep.description:
Assess a whole batch, cargo or collection quickly by handling, flagging the pieces whose material does not belong with the rest, across many items in a busy line.

Provenance Mastery read one object in full; this reads many shallowly and reliably, and picks out the exceptions for a full reading afterward. Each item still needs the user's hand on it, so the pace is limited by handling, and a large cargo is a long shift. The sweep finds outliers, not truth: a uniformly forged batch reads as uniform. Noise, fatigue and interruption erode the pass; a long day's end is read worse than its start. Nothing is proved about ownership or guilt.

[innate biological action]

Bearing Check.name: Bearing Check
Bearing Check.description:
Tell by contact whether a specific support, a beam, a ledge, a rung or a patch of floor, will bear a stated load before the user or anyone else commits weight to it.

Stress Touch perceived stress present; this tier answers a single question about stress to come. It judges the one support touched, against the load named, and nothing beyond that: it does not say what else the support is holding, whether the load will shift, or how long the support lasts under it. Hidden damage inside material the expression cannot read gives a wrong answer. Contact is required and a support already at its limit can still fail during the check.

[innate biological action]

Fatigue Memory.name: Fatigue Memory
Fatigue Memory.description:
Perceive the accumulated fatigue in a material, whether it has been over-stressed before, how close it is to the end of its life under loading and where cracks will start when it goes.

Structural Assessment mapped present stress; this tier reads the history of stress and the margin remaining. It tells whether a part is young or spent and where it is weakest, not how much longer it has in exact terms or when the final failure will come. Materials that fail without warning fatigue still fail without warning. Contact is required for each part read, and a large structure is read piece by piece. It does not strengthen or repair anything.

[innate biological action]

Safe Breach.name: Safe Breach
Safe Breach.description:
Direct exactly where and how a structure should be cut, struck or breached so that it gives way only where intended, opening a rescue path or dropping a wall without bringing down the rest.

The growth is from perceiving weakness to guiding intervention through it. The user reads the load paths under contact and names the cut line, the strike point and the order of work for whoever holds the tools. The breach is still made by real tools and effort; the expression supplies the plan, not the force. A structure with no safe line has none, and the plan is only as good as what can be read. Loads that shift once cutting begins still surprise.

[innate biological action]

Changing Load Watch.name: Changing Load Watch
Changing Load Watch.description:
Hold continuous integrity awareness over a large structure while its loads change, under fire, flood, storm or crowd, moving through it and calling failures as they begin.

Material Sovereignty assessed a wide area; this keeps that assessment live while the situation moves, through the user's own movement across the structure and through injury. The user can say which section is failing, which is next and where safe ground is at any moment. It is awareness, not support: nothing is held up by watching it, and intervention still requires contact. The structure must be within the expression's reach, and the watch narrows as the user tires.

[innate biological action]

Seam Reading.name: Seam Reading
Seam Reading.description:
Feel, through a hand laid on a joint, seam or fastening, how the real load runs through it and where it will give first.

This is the sensing side of the joining expression: a read of stress paths in one contacted join at a time, good enough to say which bolt is carrying the weight, whether a weld is bearing or merely closed, and which way a crack wants to run. It reads only what the hand touches and does not extend through a whole frame, name a material grade or replace an inspection credential. Reading while the joint is being struck or vibrated blurs the picture.

[innate biological action]

Assembly Hold.name: Assembly Hold
Assembly Hold.description:
Hold every joint along one continuous contacted assembly in its intended relationship at once, so the whole frame keeps its shape while it is cut, lifted, dragged or worked on.

Scope grows from a single joint to a connected structure the size of a vehicle frame, hull section or scaffold bay, held from a single point of contact for as long as steady effort lasts. The assembly may be moved by others while held; it may not be held from a distance, and losing contact drops the hold at once. It stabilises the joins that exist and does not bridge gaps, add material, make anything permanently unbreakable or carry loads the members themselves cannot bear.

[innate biological action]

Seam Release.name: Seam Release
Seam Release.description:
Relax the stabilisation in a chosen seam so a structure parts along that line and nowhere else, dropping a section, opening a wall or shedding a damaged member in a controlled way.

This is the reverse of holding: controlled separation through a contacted structure, with the rest of the frame kept stable while the chosen seam lets go. Refinement lets the release be timed and staged while moving, under fire or injured, and lets several seams be sequenced in one working. It does not cut sound material, disintegrate anything or throw the freed section; the piece falls as its own weight dictates, so misjudging the load endangers everyone beneath it.

[innate biological action]

Live Load Carry.name: Live Load Carry
Live Load Carry.description:
Keep a failing structure stable while people, vehicles or cargo cross or work on it, shifting the stabilisation from join to join as the load moves.

The pinnacle joins holding and structural sense in one sustained act at building or hull scale: a bridge held span by span while a column crosses, a breached hull kept sealed while the crew repairs it, a stair held during evacuation. The work follows the load and continues while the user is moving, wounded or under fire. It holds only what is there — missing material is not replaced, dead members are not revived, and the structure is no safer than the user's judgement of where the weight is going.

[innate biological action]

Cold Keep.name: Cold Keep
Cold Keep.description:
Hold the existing chill in a contacted compatible nonliving object so it warms no faster than steady effort allows.

Retention now works in both directions: a cold sample, sealed ration, coolant line or chilled pack stays near its starting temperature while held or worked. It adds no cooling, freezes nothing, does not keep living tissue cold and does not judge whether a thing is safe to eat or use. Once contact ends the object warms at its natural rate.

[innate biological action]

Thermal Handoff.name: Thermal Handoff
Thermal Handoff.description:
Move retained heat from one contacted nonliving object into another that is also in contact, warming a cold-soaked part from a hot one or drawing excess heat out of an overheating component into a sink you hold.

Transfer is the new application: heat that already exists is shifted between two things the user touches at the same time, at a pace steady effort can sustain. Nothing is generated or destroyed; the receiving object warms only as much as the source can give, at a pace set by their masses and materials. It does not draw heat from living bodies, extinguish a real fire or turn a hand into a heat shield.

[innate biological action]

Compartment Hold.name: Compartment Hold
Compartment Hold.description:
Hold the thermal state of an enclosed space — a shelter, a sealed cabin, a cold room — steady for hours while inside it.

Retention scales from an object to a bounded volume: a night shelter that keeps its warmth after the burner is out, a cold store that stays cold through a power failure, a survival compartment kept livable while help comes. Refinement lets the hold continue during sleep or ordinary work rather than demanding constant attention. Open doors, breaches and strong drafts leak faster than the hold can compensate; it neither warms nor cools the space beyond its starting state, and a space too large for one user's effort drifts.

[innate biological action]

Cooling Timeline.name: Cooling Timeline
Cooling Timeline.description:
Read the layered residual warmth across an area and place its events in order — which machine ran last, which chair was left first, which door opened after the alarm.

This is the pinnacle of mapping: thermal signatures resolved as a sequence rather than a snapshot, across a whole floor or vessel, read while walking it and while other work continues. It yields order and rough intervals, not identity or intent, and only where residual heat still exists; a fully cooled room, an area swept by strong air movement or a surface that never held warmth gives nothing. Precision falls with each hour elapsed and each layer of insulation between user and trace.

[innate biological action]

Lingering Mark.name: Lingering Mark
Lingering Mark.description:
Leave a simple composed light pattern on a receptive surface so it persists for a short while after attention leaves it.

This is the first imprint: a guide arrow, a warning glyph or a rendezvous sign that outlasts the user by minutes rather than vanishing the instant composition stops. It works on surfaces that actually take light well — pale, matte, treated or reflective — and fades faster on dark, wet or rough ones. It records nothing, carries no hidden meaning to those who cannot read the pattern and is not a permanent mark.

[innate biological action]

Moving Silhouette.name: Moving Silhouette
Moving Silhouette.description:
Compose a figure of light that moves on its own path — a guide that walks ahead down a corridor, a decoy that crosses a window, a marker that circles a hazard.

Independent motion is the new application: the figure follows a route set at composition and keeps to it while the user does other things nearby. It is convincing at a distance and in poor light, and plainly light up close or under direct inspection. It casts no shadow that bears weight, makes no sound, cannot be touched and cannot carry anything; it is not hard light and it does not think. Complex routes and more than a single figure quickly exceed steady attention.

[innate biological action]

Recorded Panel.name: Recorded Panel
Recorded Panel.description:
Imprint a full composed scene onto a prepared panel or wall so it stays and can be shown again without the user present.

A durable imprint at the scale of a message board, mural or briefing wall, holding a still composition or a short repeating sequence for days on a suitable surface. Refinement lets the imprint be laid quickly and cleanly while moving through a space, and lets a scene be corrected in place rather than redone. The imprint is light on a surface, not data: it cannot be copied by device any better than a painting can, weathers with exposure, and needs a surface that takes light well. It does not compel anyone to look, believe or obey.

[innate biological action]

Room Replay.name: Room Replay
Room Replay.description:
Project a reconstruction of recent light events in a space as a visible replay others can watch — where figures stood, how light moved, what was lit and when.

The pinnacle joins reconstruction and composition: residual optical data the expression can reach is shown back at room scale, so a team sees the sequence rather than taking the user's word for it. It works while moving and holds under distraction or injury. The replay carries only what light left behind: silhouettes, positions and movement, never faces in the dark, words, thoughts or events the ambient light has already erased. Bright daylight and long elapsed time thin it to nothing.

[innate biological action]

Muffled Tread.name: Muffled Tread
Muffled Tread.description:
Absorb the sound of your own footsteps, breathing and gear as you move, carrying a small pocket of absorption with you instead of leaving it in one place.

The absorption now travels with the user, dampening movement noise at ordinary walking pace over unfamiliar floors. It quiets what the body makes; it does not hide the user from sight, cancel the noise of a door forced or an object dropped, or erase footprints, scent or warmth. Running, climbing or fighting produces more sound than the pocket can take in.

[innate biological action]

Hushed Corridor.name: Hushed Corridor
Hushed Corridor.description:
Open a narrow clear channel of sound between yourself and one chosen source across a loud space while absorbing the noise around it, so a distant conversation or a quiet instruction reaches you alone.

Selective routing is the new application: everything along the line except the chosen source is damped, and what is spoken back along the same line reaches only the far end. It works across a crowded hall, a busy workshop or a wind-scoured roof for as long as the user can keep the line held and unobstructed. It cannot pass through solid walls, cannot pick a source the user cannot locate, and does not amplify past what the source actually produces.

[innate biological action]

Reflection Map.name: Reflection Map
Reflection Map.description:
Separate the reflections of existing sound in a space and read them as its shape, finding walls, openings, drops and large objects in darkness or smoke.

Separation turns from filtering into sensing: the echoes that ordinary hearing merges are pulled apart and placed, giving a working sense of layout, distance to surfaces and large obstacles without any light. Refinement lets the map be built while moving and while the user's own noise is absorbed. It needs some sound present — a dead-quiet space gives nothing until a sound is made — and it resolves shapes, not fine detail; a person standing still reads as an object until they move or breathe loudly.

[innate biological action]

Travelling Hush.name: Travelling Hush
Travelling Hush.description:
Hold a moving boundary of silence around a small group crossing an active environment, absorbing what the group makes while letting chosen sounds — alarms, a comrade's call, an engine — through to them.

The pinnacle combines mobile absorption, group scope and selective pass-through in one sustained working that survives the user being hurt or under fire. The boundary is only as quiet as the group's discipline: shouting, gunfire or a dropped load overload it and the excess escapes. It hides sound and nothing else, gives no protection from blast pressure, does not silence people outside it, and anyone who drifts out of the cluster is outside the hush.

[innate biological action]

Aimed Whisper.name: Aimed Whisper
Aimed Whisper.description:
Shape a quiet spoken line so it lands intelligibly on one chosen listener nearby without carrying to the people beside them.

Direction is the new element: the voice is narrowed rather than made louder, so a warning or instruction reaches the intended person at conversational range while bystanders catch only murmur. Line of sight and a still air path are needed; noise louder than the whisper still buries it, and a listener who is not paying attention still misses it. It conveys words only, with no proof of understanding and no influence beyond what the words themselves carry.

[innate biological action]

Ringing Note.name: Ringing Note
Ringing Note.description:
Find and hold the note that makes a nearby object resonate, setting a pane, panel, wire or hollow humming to locate it, rattle a latch loose or test whether a wall is solid.

Resonance turns outward onto materials: the voice sweeps within its natural range until something answers, then holds the tone to make the object vibrate visibly or audibly. It works on light, taut or hollow things at close range; thick structure, dense metal and anything heavier than a hand can shake do not respond. Small fragile items may crack, which is the extent of the harm; there is no shattering of walls or armour, no beam and no effect on living bodies beyond discomfort.

[innate biological action]

Crowd Steadying.name: Crowd Steadying
Crowd Steadying.description:
Carry the voice across a whole hall, deck or plaza so every listener hears it as if from close by, in a tone that eases startle and gives a frightened crowd something to follow.

Scope grows from a target to a gathering: instructions reach the back of a stampeding crowd and a calm tone slows the panic enough for direction to be heard. Refinement keeps the projection stable while the user moves through the crowd or is jostled. The steadying is a physiological nudge, not an order — people still choose whether to listen — and the crowd must be within hearing in open air or one connected space. Hostile listeners, sealed rooms and machine noise blunt it.

[innate biological action]

Bulkhead Call.name: Bulkhead Call
Bulkhead Call.description:
Drive the voice through solid structure — a collapsed floor, a sealed compartment, a flooded passage — so a trapped person hears intelligible words on the far side.

The pinnacle uses the material itself as the medium: the resonance is matched to the wall or rubble and the voice carried through it, sustained while the user is exhausted or digging with their hands. Words arrive; nothing comes back unless the far side can make itself heard on its own. Thick or loose fill, running water and machinery drown the call, the throat pays for every minute, and the voice remains biological — no beam, no shattering and no persuasion beyond the message spoken.

[innate biological action]

Self Steadying.name: Self Steadying
Self Steadying.description:
Turn the regulation expression on your own state, reading a rising panic, rage or grief in yourself accurately and damping the spike enough to keep working.

Self as target is the new application: the user can tell how close they are to breaking and buy a margin of composure in a moment that would otherwise take them out of a task. It is a dampener, not an eraser — the feeling remains and returns when the effort stops, fatigue narrows the margin, and repeated use in one crisis wears thin. It gives no diagnosis, no immunity to shock and no ability to feel nothing.

[innate biological action]

Tension Map.name: Tension Map
Tension Map.description:
Read the emotional temperature of a whole room or gathering at once, sensing where fear, anger or despair are clustering and who is closest to acting on it.

Perception grows from one person to a space: the user gets a working sense of the crowd's state and its hot spots, useful for choosing where to stand, whom to speak to first and when a situation is about to turn. It reads intensity and rough character, not thoughts, plans, names or the reason behind a feeling, and a practised mask or a very still person can read as calm. Larger gatherings blur into an overall tone; very crowded, noisy spaces cost more effort and give less.

[innate biological action]

Shared Calm.name: Shared Calm
Shared Calm.description:
Extend steadying regulation to a small group at once through presence and proximity rather than one-to-one contact, easing several panicking or enraged people together.

Group scope replaces the single anchored person: a knot of frightened passengers, a wounded squad, a family in shock. Refinement lets the user hold the regulation while moving among them and managing their own strain. Each person is still their own; anyone determined to stay angry or afraid resists, and no one is made to do anything. It does not reach through walls or work on a crowd larger than the user can stand among, and it drops the moment the user's own composure fails.

[innate biological action]

Crisis Vigil.name: Crisis Vigil
Crisis Vigil.description:
Sustain regulation support for one or two people through a long crisis — hours of shock, withdrawal, grief or breakdown — while reading through any mask they hold up.

The pinnacle is endurance and depth: the user sits with a person through the whole arc of a crisis, keeps them from the edge again and again, and can tell a genuine easing from a performed one. It continues while the user does other work and while tired or hurt. It remains support: the person keeps every choice, no thought is read, no memory touched, no decision made for them, and there is no diagnosis or cure. Overreach shows as the user carrying the other's state in their own body.

[innate biological action]

Recent Handling.name: Recent Handling
Recent Handling.description:
Tell from careful contact whether an object was handled recently, by one hand or several, and whether that handling was calm or agitated.

This is a narrow read layered on the foundation: recency, rough number of handlers and the emotional colour of the last contact, on a single object held in the hands. It gives no identity, no image of the handler, no sequence of events and no facts about what the object was used for. Objects handled by many people in a short span read as noise, and a thing worn by gloves or washed since reads faintly or not at all.

[innate biological action]

Residue Match.name: Residue Match
Residue Match.description:
Hold two objects and compare the impressions on them to judge whether the same person handled both.

Comparison is the new application: rather than reading one object's history, the user checks whether the emotional residue on a weapon, a note and a door handle shares a single source. It gives a match or a mismatch with a felt degree of confidence, never a name, a face or a testimony-grade claim, and a strong recent handler can mask a fainter earlier one. Objects handled long ago, cleaned or passed through many hands lose the signature and give no answer.

[innate biological action]

Room Sweep.name: Room Sweep
Room Sweep.description:
Read residue across a whole surface or room by contact with its floor, walls and fixtures, placing where people stood, moved, waited or struggled.

Scope grows from an object to a scene: laying hands on the room builds a picture of who was where and what was felt in that spot, useful for reconstructing a fight, a meeting or a flight. Refinement lets the sweep be done quickly while others work the same room. It yields positions and emotional tone, not identities, words or the order of events unless a strong impression sets a clear before and after. Heavily trafficked places read as a blur, and open ground with no surfaces to touch gives nothing.

[innate biological action]

Sediment Reading.name: Sediment Reading
Sediment Reading.description:
Reach through the recent layers on a long-held object to an impression laid down years ago, peeling back handlers in order until the wanted stratum is found.

The pinnacle is depth in time: sustained contact over a long sitting lets the user work down through the accumulated residue of an heirloom, a ship's wheel or a cell door to something old and buried. Each layer costs effort and the deepest come faint and fragmentary, the feeling of an event more often than any picture of it. It still yields no names, no facts a court would accept, no memory stolen from anyone, and objects remade, burned or long untouched by hands have nothing to give.

[innate biological action]

Tissue Read.name: Tissue Read
Tissue Read.description:
Feel, through deliberate contact, whether a known injury is actually recovering, stalled or getting worse beneath the surface.

This is a limited sensing step for the recovery expression: a read of the living field at the site of one injury the user can touch, enough to tell healing from failing and to notice heat, swelling or dead tissue that the eye misses. It is not a medical qualification, does not name a cause, find a toxin or read a whole body, and it treats nothing by itself; it tells the user where to place the support they already have.

[innate biological action]

Clot Support.name: Clot Support
Clot Support.description:
Support the body's own clotting and vessel constriction at a serious bleed under contact, slowing blood loss while proper treatment is applied.

Haemorrhage control is the new application: pressure and packing work faster and hold better because the tissue is being helped to do what it is already trying to do. It buys time on a wound that would otherwise kill in minutes; it does not close a severed vessel, replace lost blood, work on internal bleeding the user cannot reach with a hand, or substitute for surgery. Holding it through a long extraction drains the user in proportion to the wound.

[innate biological action]

Clearance Support.name: Clearance Support
Clearance Support.description:
Support a patient's own clearing of a toxin, venom or infection, keeping failing organs working while the body does the removal.

Scope moves from wounds to whole-body burden: the user sustains kidney, liver and immune effort through a poisoning or a septic crisis under continuous contact. Refinement lets the support be maintained while moving a patient or splitting attention across a small number of them. It is not an antidote, does not identify what the toxin is, cannot clear what the body has no way to clear, and a dose beyond the body's survivable range still kills. The user's own body carries a proportional share of the strain.

[innate biological action]

Nerve Regrowth.name: Nerve Regrowth
Nerve Regrowth.description:
Support the slow regrowth of nerve and other complex tissue where a viable path for it exists, over repeated sessions across weeks.

The pinnacle reaches tissue the body normally gives up on: a crushed nerve, a spinal injury with intact cord, a burn that would scar rigid. Regrowth still happens at the body's pace, only faster and cleaner, and only where living tissue remains to grow from. No organ is regrown, no lost limb returns, nothing dead is revived, and there is no resurrection or refilling of anything. Each session costs the user heavily, strain builds over the course, and a patient without reserves cannot be carried past their own limits.

[innate biological action]

Self Gauge.name: Self Gauge
Self Gauge.description:
Read your own neural strain accurately — how much fatigue, pain load and attention are left before your body or judgement fails.

Self-monitoring is the new application: the user knows when they are about to make a tired mistake, when a pain is masking an injury and how far a push can go before collapse. The read is honest but not protective; it removes no pain, adds no endurance and does not stop the body from failing when the gauge says it will. Shock and adrenaline can lag the read by a few breaths.

[innate biological action]

Rotation Read.name: Rotation Read
Rotation Read.description:
Read the neural strain of a group at close range and order them by remaining capacity — who can go on, who needs rest now, who is hiding an injury.

The sense widens from one person to a team: a fair ranking of exhaustion, pain and cognitive load across a squad, a work crew or a set of casualties, good enough to decide rotation and priority. It reads state, never thought, and it gives no diagnosis beyond where the strain sits. Anyone outside close range or behind cover drops out of the ranking, and a very large group blurs into a rough sort rather than an order.

[innate biological action]

Creature Strain.name: Creature Strain
Creature Strain.description:
Extend the sense to non-sapient animals and unfamiliar species, reading an animal's pain, fear and exhaustion to handle, treat or avoid it safely.

A new target class: livestock, guard animals, wildlife and species whose bodies the user has never studied, read for stress and injury at close range or on contact. Refinement lets the user keep the read while working on a struggling animal or moving through a herd. It reveals where the strain is, not why, and offers no command over the animal, no calming of it and no protection from it. Creatures with very alien nervous systems read faintly or not at all.

[innate biological action]

Rubble Reach.name: Rubble Reach
Rubble Reach.description:
Locate living beings through collapsed structure, rubble or a sealed compartment by their neural stress signatures, telling the living from the dead and the failing from the stable.

The pinnacle carries the sense through barriers that stop sight and sound, across a search area the size of a fallen building, while the user is climbing, digging or hurt. It gives position, rough count and who is closest to dying — enough to choose where to dig first. It does not communicate, heal, sedate or move anyone, offers no read on thoughts, and depth, dense material and a great many signals at once degrade it to a faint sense of presence.

[innate biological action]

Shelved Input.name: Shelved Input
Shelved Input.description:
Wall off a single distracting input — a pain, a fear, an alarm, a heckler — into a held partition so the primary task keeps its full attention.

Partitioning turns inward on distraction: the input is still there and still felt, but it stops pulling at the working thread for as long as steady effort holds the wall. It shelves one thing at a time, does not remove pain or fear, does not stop a real injury from worsening while ignored, and collapses when the primary task itself becomes overwhelming.

[innate biological action]

Standing Model.name: Standing Model
Standing Model.description:
Build and hold a structured mental model of a problem — a case, a machine, a negotiation — with its linked facts and open questions, keeping it intact across a working day without notes.

Persistence is the new application: the model survives interruptions, sleep loss and other tasks, and can be picked up where it was left. It holds what the user actually learned, linked as they understood it; it invents nothing, corrects no false premise on its own and does not become perfect recall of raw detail. Fatigue frays the edges first, and a second model of equal size cannot be held at the same time.

[innate biological action]

Twin Working.name: Twin Working
Twin Working.description:
Run two dissimilar skilled tasks at full quality at the same time — piloting while negotiating, treating a patient while directing triage — each on its own partition.

The partitions now carry practised skills rather than lines of thought, so both tasks get real competence instead of split attention. Refinement lets the pairing hold under stress, movement or injury. Both tasks must be ones the user actually knows; the ability grants no skill and does not make either task faster than its own nature allows. Any task needing the hands is limited by having only two of them, and a third demanding task breaks the pairing.

[innate biological action]

Running Ledger.name: Running Ledger
Running Ledger.description:
Hold a live model of a whole operation — many people, positions, reports and timings — reconciling incoming information in parallel and flagging contradictions as they arrive.

The pinnacle scales the standing model to a moving situation: an evacuation, a search grid, a multi-team job, tracked as it changes and kept coherent while the user is in the field, under fire or hurt. It holds and links only what is reported or observed; it does not know what no one told it, does not predict what has not happened and reads no minds. When input exceeds what the user can take in, the ledger drops threads, and the user may not notice which.

[innate biological action]

Cued Recall.name: Cued Recall
Cued Recall.description:
When a pattern you have actually seen before recurs, recall exactly where and when you met it — the page, the face, the door, the phrase.

Recall is the new application: recognition now comes with its source, so the user can say where a detail was previously encountered rather than only that it feels familiar. It reaches only what the user genuinely observed and attended to, gives nothing for things never seen, and fades for observations that were casual or long ago. It supplies no hidden facts and cannot say whether the remembered source was truthful.

[innate biological action]

Habit Signature.name: Habit Signature
Habit Signature.description:
Recognise the individual habits in a piece of work or a sequence of actions — a fighter's timing, a coder's structure, a forger's hand — and tell whether two samples share a maker.

Pattern recognition applied to authorship: the user matches signatures across samples with a felt degree of confidence. It gives a match, not a name, unless the user already knows whose habits those are; it can be fooled by deliberate imitation and by very generic work, and it needs enough of each sample to carry a habit. It is not foresight and not a judgement about which of two accounts is true.

[innate biological action]

Absent Piece.name: Absent Piece
Absent Piece.description:
Notice what is missing from a pattern — the guard who is not on rotation, the entry gone from a ledger, the silence where a machine should be running.

Recognition of absence is a qualitatively different act from recognition of presence, and it is what this tier grants. Refinement lets the user hold the expected pattern in mind across a whole site or record and check it while moving through and while other work goes on. It finds gaps only against patterns the user has actually established; an unfamiliar system has no baseline, a well-covered gap still reads as whole, and it says nothing about why the piece is missing or where it went.

[innate biological action]

Scene Playback.name: Scene Playback
Scene Playback.description:
Replay a scene you observed in ordered detail, re-examining what your senses actually took in for details you did not consciously note at the time.

The pinnacle is retrospective recall of raw observation: a room, a conversation, a fight, revisited later for the badge on a sleeve, the sound behind the door, the face at the back. It carries only what the user's own senses reached — nothing outside their field of view, nothing too far away to hear — and is sharpest for recent scenes, though it works under load. It is not perfect memory of a life, cannot resolve what was blurred at the time and offers no truth about what the recalled people intended.

[innate biological action]

Dimmed Features.name: Dimmed Features
Dimmed Features.description:
Shade your own face and hands so identifying features are hard to make out at a glance in ordinary light, while your presence itself is not hidden.

This is shadowed presentation rather than concealment: the user is seen but not readily recognised in a passing look or a crowd. It works while standing or walking calmly in even light; a direct stare from close by, bright light on the face, a recording device or a person who knows the user well defeats it. It does not alter voice, gait, build or clothing, and it does not make anyone forget having seen the user.

[innate biological action]

Companion Shade.name: Companion Shade
Companion Shade.description:
Extend concealment to one other person in contact or at your side, keeping a child, a casualty or an ally softened into the shadow with you as you move slowly through cover.

The expression now covers a second body: two outlines merged with the surroundings at a walking pace through shadow and clutter. The companion's own movement, noise and light — a torch, a bright coat, a cry — break the cover as surely as the user's would. Bright light, open ground and a searcher looking directly at the pair defeat it, and the range is arm's reach; anyone who steps away is on their own.

[innate biological action]

Overlooked Cache.name: Overlooked Cache
Overlooked Cache.description:
Conceal a stationary object, doorway or cache rather than a person, making it fall out of notice in a room that is looked at but not searched.

A new target class: a bundle in a corner, a hatch in a floor, a body under a tarp, softened into the room's arrangement so a glance slides past it. Refinement lets the effect be set and left for a stretch of time while the user is elsewhere. It holds against passive observation only — a deliberate search, a hand laid on the spot, a light shone directly on it, a scanner or a dog finds it — and objects that make noise, heat or scent are not hidden in those senses. Large or moving things exceed it.

[innate biological action]

Moving Veil.name: Moving Veil
Moving Veil.description:
Hold concealment for yourself and a small group while moving at speed or in flight through changing light and under active search.

The pinnacle takes the bending of light and attention off the still figure and onto a moving team crossing a lit street, a searchlight sweep or open sky, with the user managing the veil while hurt or hurried. The group must stay tight and disciplined; a runner who breaks formation or a bright piece of gear is visible. Active detection — scanners, thermal sight, dogs, a searcher who knows where to look — degrades it quickly, sustained use wears it thin, and it never hides sound, heat, scent or tracks.

[innate biological action]

Braced Contact.name: Braced Contact
Braced Contact.description:
Commit the mantle into one hardened contact surface — a palm, forearm or shoulder — to catch, hold or shove a single heavy object or incoming blow.

At this practiced stage the hardening is momentary and local: it covers the point of contact, not the whole body, and it does not answer a second threat arriving from another side. Weight the body cannot brace behind still moves the user; a falling load still needs somewhere safe to go. No area protection, no work on others yet, and no repair of what the contact already damaged.

[Elyri embodied action]

Escort Sheath.name: Escort Sheath
Escort Sheath.description:
Draw the mantle out along a moving group — evacuees, a stretcher party, a work crew — and keep it wrapped around them while they and the user move through debris, falling material or scattered fire.

Expert scope is motion: the sheath keeps its shape while the user walks, climbs or flies with the group, and it re-closes as people shift inside it. The group must stay within the user's reach of field; anyone who runs ahead leaves the sheath. Splitting the group divides the protection, and a heavy concentrated strike on one side is met by that side alone. Not a sealed pressure envelope, and no coverage of anyone the user cannot see or feel.

[Elyri embodied action]

Pressure Stand.name: Pressure Stand
Pressure Stand.description:
Plant the mantle as a fixed wall against a sustained environmental load — a pressure front, a shifting collapse, floodwater, a spreading burn — and hold it for as long as others need to work or clear out behind it.

Master scope is duration under a load that does not stop: the mantle takes the pressure continuously instead of meeting single strikes. The stance is stationary; stepping back or turning to another task drops the wall. The overuse ladder advances with every stretch the wall is held, and a load that exceeds the core's support pushes through rather than stopping. Not a structural repair, not breathable air and not immunity for the user.

[Elyri embodied action]

Remote Sheath.name: Remote Sheath
Remote Sheath.description:
Set a self-holding protective sheath on another person, an animal or a vehicle and keep it maintained through the field from beyond arm's reach while they move away from you.

Pinnacle scope is separation: the sheath persists without contact, and the user can hold it while stationary or moving slowly, tracking the carrier by field sense. One sheath at a time; it thins with distance and fails when the user is struck hard, loses concentration or drops a rung on the ladder. It protects the carrier from impact and heat; it is not a life-support bubble, cannot pass to a second carrier, and cannot go where the user has no field sense of it.

[Elyri embodied action]

Working Pulse.name: Working Pulse
Working Pulse.description:
Release a short, low-output coherent pulse for a working task — cauterise a wound, weld a seam, cut a cable, score a mark, or fire a visible warning across open ground.

Practiced scope is restraint of output: the pulse is brief and narrow, held below the intensity that would breach or kill, and delivered from a still hand at close range. It cannot be sustained, swept or split; it is not a fighting lance. Working precision depends on the user's actual craft or medical knowledge of the job, and a pulse aimed at living tissue without that knowledge burns rather than treats.

[Elyri embodied action]

Fanned Sweep.name: Fanned Sweep
Fanned Sweep.description:
Spread coherent output into a wide, low-intensity fan and sweep it across an arc to clear light debris, drive a crowd or animal pack back, flash-heat a surface, or light a broad area.

Expert scope trades depth for breadth: the fan covers many targets at once with force that pushes and scalds rather than cuts. It cannot breach structure, discriminate one target within the arc, or be held without the user standing still and paying core stability for every pass. Anyone inside the arc is affected, allies included; a fan aimed at people who cannot get clear becomes injury, not persuasion.

[Elyri embodied action]

Sustained Breach Cut.name: Sustained Breach Cut
Sustained Breach Cut.description:
Hold a continuous cutting emission for long enough to breach heavy structure — a hull plate, a bulkhead, a rockfall, a sealed blast door — while walking the cut along its line.

Master scope is uninterrupted duration: the cut stays coherent while the user moves along it, and it continues through material that would defeat a single lance. Every span of the cut costs fatigue and the overuse ladder, and the user cannot fight, fly or protect anyone while cutting. Thick, layered or actively cooled material slows the line and may stop it. Molten edges, pressure release and what lies behind the breach are hazards the cut does not manage.

[Elyri embodied action]

Parted Emission.name: Parted Emission
Parted Emission.description:
Divide coherent output into two or three independently aimed and independently held emissions at once — one cutting, one holding a breach open, one warning off an approach — each placed by field sense rather than line of sight alone.

Pinnacle scope is simultaneity: separate emissions with separate purposes and separate intensities, held together and shifted as the situation changes.
