It cannot be held indefinitely, breaks down on open ground or when a fourth attacker joins, and guarantees no counter; a thrown object or a firearm ignores the geometry entirely.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Stopping Hit.name: Stopping Hit
Stopping Hit.description:
From an accurate defensive read, deliver one disciplined strike to a chosen structural target such as the knee, liver or jaw, intended to end the exchange rather than continue it.

The new element is choice: the strike lands on the part you named, with the force you intended and no more, which keeps it inside arena and legal norms of stoppage rather than killing. It is one strike on one exposed target; a covered target means no hit, armour over the target means nothing happens, and a missed read leaves you extended. It does not chain into further strikes.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Empty Hand Answer.name: Empty Hand Answer
Empty Hand Answer.description:
Meet an attacker armed with a blade, baton or sidearm at contact range bare-handed, controlling the weapon arm while moving off the line, and disarm or disable them within a single exchange.

This is the first tier that addresses a weapon at all, and only at arm's length: a firearm beyond reach cannot be answered, two armed attackers are not covered, and a powered or energised blade still cuts if the control slips. Injury to you remains real. The outcome is the weapon out of their hand or the attacker unable to continue; it is not a killing technique and does not pretend to be.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Base and Frame.name: Base and Frame
Base and Frame.description:
Keep a low balanced base and use forearm and hip frames so that a single opponent cannot take you down or pin you, and work back to your feet from any hold they do get.

This covers standing balance and escape from one opponent's hold; it does not reverse the hold into control of them, and a much heavier opponent can still drag you down through it. Escaping costs a moment and a step, not nothing, and it stops when a second person takes hold.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Ground Transition Chain.name: Ground Transition Chain
Ground Transition Chain.description:
Move through a chain of positions on the ground, from underneath a single opponent to a stable top position, keeping control through their scrambling.

What grew is continuity: instead of one hold or escape, you keep position through several changes without giving the opponent a clean reset. It is one opponent on ground that lets you move; a second person standing over you ends it, and a hard, cluttered or sloping surface makes every transition slower and riskier. Sustaining it drains stamina steadily.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Standing Pin.name: Standing Pin
Standing Pin.description:
Pin a resisting person upright against a wall, rail or vehicle so that they cannot strike, draw a weapon or run, while keeping their airway clear and one of your hands briefly free for a restraint, a call or a check.

This needs a solid surface and a person in roughly your own size class; a much larger or reshaped opponent walks out of it. It holds one person and keeps them safe, which is the point of the Nonlethal Control partnership: no choke, no joint destruction. The free hand is a moment, not a stance, and a second attacker ends the pin.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Weight Class Reversal.name: Weight Class Reversal
Weight Class Reversal.description:
Defeat the hold of a heavier or stronger opponent by leverage and timing rather than strength, and reverse it into your own top control.

The lane's foundation warns that a stronger opponent may defeat the attempt; at this tier that ceases to be true for an ordinary bipedal body, however heavy. It still fails against overwhelming mass such as an Olyth reshaped to full bulk, machinery or a braced group, and the reversal costs a large share of your stamina, so it is one reversal per exchange, not a way of fighting all day. Holding what you gain still depends on position.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Reach Check.name: Reach Check
Reach Check.description:
Hold one attacker at the staff's full length with tip checks and short thrusts, so that they cannot close without meeting the end of it.

This is distance management against a single attacker on open floor with a staff actually in your hands. It does not strike them down, does not work once they are inside the reach, and a firearm or anything thrown ignores it. In a corridor narrower than the staff the checks become jabs and lose their authority.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Improvised Pole.name: Improvised Pole
Improvised Pole.description:
Apply the staff curriculum at full competence to any rigid length actually to hand: a pipe, a pole, a tool haft, a rail or strut torn free.

The new medium is the point; the object's real weight, balance and fragility remain. A flimsy length breaks on the first hard contact, a heavy one tires you fast, and a short one is a club, not a staff. It creates nothing; there must be an object in reach, and taking it up costs a moment in which you are unarmed.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Corridor Hold.name: Corridor Hold
Corridor Hold.description:
Hold a doorway or corridor against several attackers with the staff, reading which of them will commit and meeting only that one while the reach denies the rest.

With Defensive Reading the read is trustworthy against about three attackers at a chokepoint no wider than the staff's span. It fails on open ground, when anyone flanks through another way in, or against thrown objects and shots that pass over the staff. The hold lasts as long as your arms and breath do, which is minutes rather than an hour.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Disarming Bind.name: Disarming Bind
Disarming Bind.description:
Bind an armed opponent's weapon with the staff and strip it from their hands, whether a blade, a baton or a short firearm held at contact range.

This takes one weapon from one opponent who has extended or committed; a weapon kept back is not reachable. A firearm at range is unaffected. Against an energised or cutting edge the bind is a gamble: a staff the weapon can cut through is lost, and the weapon is not. The opponent is disarmed, not disabled, and may still fight bare-handed.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Guard and Retreat.name: Guard and Retreat
Guard and Retreat.description:
Keep one attacker off you with your familiar blade held in guard while backing towards an exit you have chosen.

This is defence and distance with a blade actually in hand, against one attacker who respects the edge. It makes no strike, gives no ground advantage back, and does nothing against a firearm or a second attacker coming from the side. It ends at the exit or when your back meets something you did not plan for.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Two-Line Fence.name: Two-Line Fence
Two-Line Fence.description:
Hold off two blade-armed opponents by managing lines so that only one of them can engage at any moment.

The scope grew from one opponent to two, and it works while you keep moving; standing still lets them coordinate. Three opponents overwhelm it, a thrown object or a shot passes through it, and it produces no counter of its own. Fatigue is real, so it is a way to reach a wall, a door or help, not a way to win alone.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Stoppage Cut.name: Stoppage Cut
Stoppage Cut.description:
Deliver a controlled cut or thrust to the target the situation permits, such as a limb, a guard or a piece of equipment, so that a bout or an encounter ends by surrender, incapacitation or stoppage rather than by a killing wound.

The narrator honours the choice of target and depth: the blade lands where you named and no deeper. It needs an actual opening in one opponent, and an opponent who will not yield after a disabling cut is still a fight. Armour over the target stops the cut, and choosing restraint costs you a moment in which they may act. This keeps the lane inside arena judging and law; it is not a way to hurt someone more efficiently.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Unfamiliar Edge Adoption.name: Unfamiliar Edge Adoption
Unfamiliar Edge Adoption.description:
Take up any bladed weapon actually available, whatever its design, length or energised edge, and fight with it at your full competence from the first exchange.

The lane's foundation demands a familiar weapon; this tier removes that limit. The weapon's real characteristics still apply: a powered edge needs its controls found and its charge is finite, a long blade needs room, a broken one stays broken. It grants no House technique and does not include weapons that are not blades. Adopting the weapon takes the moment of picking it up, and it must physically be there.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Clear and Reload.name: Clear and Reload
Clear and Reload.description:
Clear a stoppage or feed fault in your held familiar firearm and reload or swap its cell while keeping sight of the threat, without stepping out of cover.

This needs actual spare ammunition or a charged cell on you; it produces none. A weapon that is physically broken, locked out or empty of everything stays that way, and the moments it takes are moments in which you are not firing. It covers one weapon of a type you know.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Cover to Cover.name: Cover to Cover
Cover to Cover.description:
Fire accurately at a single moving target while you yourself move between cover positions, without stopping to plant.

What grew is accuracy while both parties move; it is single, aimed shots, not automatic fire, and covers one target you can see. Shooting behind you or through smoke is not part of it. Ammunition, recoil and the real range of the weapon remain, and a stumble on bad ground still spoils the shot.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Component Hit.name: Component Hit
Component Hit.description:
Put a round into a specific chosen part rather than a body: a weapon hand, a drone's rotor or mount, a vehicle's tyre or lift unit, a lock, a light.

With Targeted Precision the narrator honours the named part: the round strikes it, not the person or the whole. It needs line of sight, the part within the weapon's real accuracy at that range, and a part big enough to be hit at all. Disabling a person this way is still a wound with consequences, and hardened parts may take the hit without failing.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Foreign Weapon Read.name: Foreign Weapon Read
Foreign Weapon Read.description:
Pick up any firearm actually present, read its controls, feed, safety and state by inspection within a moment, and use it at your full competence.

The foundation demands a familiar weapon; this tier removes that limit for any hand-held firearm, including exotic or House-pattern designs. A weapon locked to another user, empty, or damaged stays so; reading it tells you that rather than fixing it. It grants no knowledge of who owns it and no authorisation to use it, and heavy or mounted weapons need more than a moment.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Close Walk.name: Close Walk
Close Walk.description:
Walk one consenting charge through a crowd or street with your body between them and the most likely direction of threat, steering them by touch and a quiet word.

This is one charge, on foot, in a space you can read as you walk. It does not stop a crowd, does not spot a threat you cannot see, and does not command anyone else present. If the charge stops cooperating the walk ends; it is not a restraint.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Vehicle Transfer.name: Vehicle Transfer
Vehicle Transfer.description:
Move one charge into or out of a vehicle, transit pod or doorway, the most exposed moment of an escort, with cover, timing and sequence rehearsed so the gap in protection is as short as it can be.

The scope grew to the transition points that a walking escort cannot cover. The vehicle or doorway must actually be there and usable; there is no vehicle summoned. One charge, one transfer, and a threat already inside the vehicle is not addressed by this. Companions present help only if they cooperate; you do not command them.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Split Party Escort.name: Split Party Escort
Split Party Escort.description:
Escort two or three consenting charges through a hostile area, tracking all of them and choosing when to keep them together and when to separate them to reduce exposure.

With Group Combat Awareness the count of charges grows and the routing becomes deliberate. Charges must follow direction; a charge who will not is one you can no longer cover. More than three thins protection to nothing, and this is not command over allies or bystanders. A route that does not exist cannot be taken.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Decoy Departure.name: Decoy Departure
Decoy Departure.description:
Mislead pursuers about where a charge has gone by route change, a stand-in or timing, so that the charge leaves an area unseen while attention follows the wrong direction.

This is a qualitatively different outcome from moving a charge under cover: the pursuers lose the charge rather than follow them. It needs a plausible alternative to exist in the scene and a moment when the pursuers cannot see the charge directly; a pursuer with eyes on them is not fooled. A stand-in must be a willing person, not a disguise or a working. It buys a departure, not permanent safety, and a drone or tracker on the charge defeats it.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Wrist and Walk.name: Wrist and Walk
Wrist and Walk.description:
Take one person's arm in a walking escort hold that guides them out of a space without pain or injury, whether they are drunk, distressed or merely unwelcome.

This is guiding, not dragging: it works on a person who resists passively and breaks the moment they fight seriously, which is when the lane's other holds apply. One person, on their feet, on ground they can walk. It does not calm them and gives you no authority they must obey.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Crisis Hold.name: Crisis Hold
Crisis Hold.description:
Restrain one person in acute distress, panicking, intoxicated or harming themselves, safely until they calm or help arrives, monitoring their breathing and circulation throughout.

What grew is duration and care: this hold is meant to be kept for minutes, and it releases or changes if breathing is compromised. It is for a person who is a danger to themselves or others through distress, not for a committed armed attacker. Their strength, their weight and the ground still matter, and it does not treat whatever caused the crisis.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Castro Family Pin.name: Castro Family Pin
Castro Family Pin.description:
Apply the Castro family's protected ground restraint, which immobilises a stronger resisting adult through position rather than strength while keeping airway, neck and every joint safe, for as long as it needs to be held.

This is the protected tradition, not the public style, and it may be named as such. It holds one person on flat ground and is intended for protection and release, never for punishment; the person comes out of it unharmed unless they injure themselves fighting it. A second attacker breaks it, a trained observer recognises it, and it does not work on a body whose anatomy the pin was not built for.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Armed Subject Hold.name: Armed Subject Hold
Armed Subject Hold.description:
Restrain one person holding a blade or sidearm at contact range, controlling the weapon and the person together so that the weapon leaves their hand and they are held without lasting harm to either of you.

This is the lane's answer to a weapon, and it stays nonlethal on both sides: the intended end is the weapon on the floor and the person restrained and breathing. Contact range only; a shot fired during the attempt is still a shot, and a second armed person is not covered. It is protective and consent-aware in purpose, meant for the moment a situation turns, and it releases when the threat ends. Against a powered edge a slip cuts you, not them.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Gap Close.name: Gap Close
Gap Close.description:
Cross the distance to one opponent who is trying to keep you at range in a single committed step, arriving inside their reach with your guard up.

This is one step against one opponent on open floor; it does not include a strike and does not undo a weapon in their hand, which the step still has to pass. On slick or cluttered ground the step is slower and may be read. If they retreat as fast as you close, you have gained nothing but breath spent.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Corner Drive.name: Corner Drive
Corner Drive.description:
Drive one opponent to a wall, ring edge or corner by angled pressure, taking away their retreat one step at a time.

What grew is the goal: not contact but the removal of the opponent's space, which in an arena means a ring condition the judge can call. It works on one opponent who is on foot; a flier, or one who circles faster than you cut, is not cornered. It costs sustained effort and leaves you exposed if a second opponent comes from the flank.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Storm Cadence.name: Storm Cadence
Storm Cadence.description:
Take up the Genesis tradition's storm-like forward pressure: a sustained rhythm of strikes and steps that denies one opponent any moment to reset, breaking their guard by tempo rather than force.

This is the protected form of the pressure style and may be named as such. With Strike Discipline every strike in the rhythm is placed rather than thrown, so the cadence does not blow itself out early. It lasts while breath lasts, a few exchanges, and works on one opponent; a disciplined defender who yields ground without breaking turns it into a chase, and a weapon in their hand is met by the rhythm, not removed by it. When it stops you are spent.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Cordon Breakthrough.name: Cordon Breakthrough
Cordon Breakthrough.description:
Press through a line of two or three opponents, a doorway guard or a cordon, by pressure and momentum, breaking through rather than fighting each one.

The scope grew from one opponent to a line, and the outcome is passage, not victory: you arrive on the far side winded and the line is disordered behind you. It works on two or three lightly armed or unprepared people. A braced line with shields or a locked formation stops it, a firearm in the line is still fired, and a wall of bodies deeper than three closes over you.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Braced Block.name: Braced Block
Braced Block.description:
Set your feet and guard to take one heavy blow, a swung object or a charging body, and stay standing where you were.

This is one blow, seen coming, taken on a guard or on actual equipment you hold; the impact is still felt and can still injure through the guard. A vehicle, a fall or a blast is not blocked, and a blow from behind is not seen. It holds your position; it does not move you forward or answer back.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Redline Anchor.name: Redline Anchor
Redline Anchor.description:
Hold the anchor position of Dravon's Redline formation doctrine, the fixed point that trained companions form on, reading the pressure across the whole line and shifting your own segment to keep it closed.

This is the protected doctrine and may be named as such. With companions who know the Redline, the line holds and shifts as one; without them, you hold your own segment with the read and nothing more, because a line is not conjured from untrained people and this is not command over them. The line breaks when flanked or when the anchor tires, and against fire from beyond its reach it is only cover.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Redline Withdrawal.name: Redline Withdrawal
Redline Withdrawal.description:
Conduct a fighting withdrawal in the Redline sequence, stepping back so that the line never opens, from a position that has become untenable to one that can be held.

The new outcome is a line that moves without breaking. It needs trained Dravon-doctrine companions to be a line at all; alone, it is your own disciplined withdrawal with the ground read ahead of you. It is slow, it costs the ground you give, and it does not disengage from an opponent faster than you. Untrained allies may follow your example but are not formed by it.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Angle Reset.name: Angle Reset
Angle Reset.description:
Recover a lost angle in the middle of an exchange with a short step and a change of grip, so that a failed action does not leave you open.

This is one recovery per exchange against one opponent, with a blade actually in hand. It does not produce a counter and it does not undo a hit already taken; it puts you back in guard. If the ground does not allow the step, the reset is only the grip.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Blind Side Entry.name: Blind Side Entry
Blind Side Entry.description:
Move to one opponent's blind side, off their lead and behind their guard, during the moment their own action commits them.

What grew is position: you end the exchange somewhere they must turn to find. It reads the opponent's visible movement only, and against one who does not commit there is no moment to use. It is one opponent; a second one sees you go. Cluttered ground or a wall at your back removes the room the move needs.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Wayline Reading.name: Wayline Reading
Wayline Reading.description:
Use the Wayline of Rux Corsair, the protected House form, to read an opponent's line of intent from their footwork and commit your blade to where they will be before their action completes.

This is the protected tradition and may be named as such. It reads only what the body shows; it is not prediction of hidden intent, and it fails against an opponent whose feet you cannot see. Another Wayline practitioner can feint the line, and a weapon that strikes from beyond blade reach gives no footwork to read. One opponent, one commitment; the body still has to arrive on time.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Wayline Crossing.name: Wayline Crossing
Wayline Crossing.description:
Engage two blade opponents at once along the Wayline, moving through them on a line that neither can follow, so that each commitment against one opens the other.

The scope grew from one opponent to two, and the outcome is control of the exchange rather than survival of it. Three opponents break the line, as does a space too narrow to cross. It costs heavy stamina and lasts a few exchanges. It does not deliver a killing stroke by design; in an arena it ends on stoppage or surrender, and outside one it ends when the line does.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Retreat Cut-Off.name: Retreat Cut-Off
Retreat Cut-Off.description:
Step to close one opponent's line of retreat instead of chasing them along it.

This covers one opponent, on the ground, in a space where their exit is visible to you; it does not stop a flier, a vehicle or a person who has more than one way out. It creates no strike and no contact, only a moment where they must choose again, and on bad footing the step may cost you the moment instead.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Running Exchange.name: Running Exchange
Running Exchange.description:
Trade blade actions with one opponent while both of you are moving at speed through streets or corridors, without stopping to set your feet.

What grew is fighting at a run rather than after one. Footing, corners, bystanders and traffic are real hazards in it, and a stumble is an opening. It is one opponent; a flier or a vehicle outpaces it, and it still guarantees no contact. Stamina goes quickly.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Redcourt Chase.name: Redcourt Chase
Redcourt Chase.description:
Pursue a fleeing opponent in the Veltrax Redcourt tradition across obstacles and changes of level at a pace that closes the gap, and arrive with breath and guard intact.

This is the protected House tradition and may be named as such. It is a pursuit within your own running and climbing; flight, a vehicle or a door that locks behind them escapes it. A pursuit that turns is a fight, and the Redcourt does not make you stronger in it, only ready. It does not force the opponent's choices and it stays mindful of bystanders in the way.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Redcourt Intercept.name: Redcourt Intercept
Redcourt Intercept.description:
Read the ground and the opponent's flight to predict where they will emerge, and cut across to meet them there rather than follow them.

The new outcome is interception: arriving ahead of the opponent instead of behind them. It works from what you can actually see of the ground and the district; an exit you do not know about is one they can take. One opponent on foot. A flier or a vehicle is not intercepted on foot. A wrong read leaves you at the wrong place with the chase lost.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Body Cover.name: Body Cover
Body Cover.description:
Cover one consenting charge with your own body against a thrown object, a blast or a burst of fire, turning so that your back and any armour you wear take it.

This is one charge, one moment; the injury to you is real and is the point. It does not reduce the harm, does not shield against anything from the side you are not turned to, and does not include heat resistance or injury transfer. If the charge moves out from behind you, the cover is gone.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Escort in Motion.name: Escort in Motion
Escort in Motion.description:
Keep one charge covered while both of you move at a walk or a jog through a crowd or a hostile street, repositioning yourself around them as threats change side.

What grew is coverage in motion. It covers one charge well; a second is covered thinly and a third not at all. It does not command anyone else, does not clear the crowd, and a threat from above is met only if you have seen it. The charge must keep moving with you.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Pain Ledger.name: Pain Ledger
Pain Ledger.description:
Take a hit meant for a charge and, in Volen's doctrine of pain as information, read from your own pain exactly what was struck and how badly, staying on your feet and reporting your true condition rather than a brave one.

This is the protected Volen doctrine and may be named as such. It does not reduce the injury; it keeps you functional and informed for the moment after it, which is what a charge needs. A killing hit still kills. With Group Combat Awareness you keep track of the other threats while you take it. It works for one hit at a time and does not remove the need for treatment afterwards.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Last Line Stand.name: Last Line Stand
Last Line Stand.description:
Hold as the last barrier between a small group of charges and a threat when there is no exit, keeping all of them behind you in a corner, an alcove or a doorway.

The scope grew to several charges, three practical and five at the edge, and the outcome is that everything comes to you first. It lasts as long as your body does, which is not long against sustained fire, and it ends when help arrives, the threat stops or you go down. It is not an assault, does not command the charges beyond keeping them behind you, and a threat that reaches past you is theirs to face.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Lift Away.name: Lift Away
Lift Away.description:
Disengage upward from a ground threat in one motion of ordinary Starian flight, to a height beyond an arm or a blade.

This needs overhead space and works against one threat on the ground; a firearm still reaches you, and carrying a person or a load may keep you too low or too slow. It is an exit, not a position of advantage, and in an enclosed room it is only a hop.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Vertical Break.name: Vertical Break
Vertical Break.description:
Break a pursuit in the air with a sudden climb or dive so that one flying pursuer overshoots and loses the line.

What grew is the use of the third dimension against another flier. It works on one pursuer who is following, not on one who is waiting. Airspace limits and the ceiling of the space are real, as is the stamina a hard climb costs, and a diving break near the ground ends on the ground if misjudged.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Sustained Air Bout.name: Sustained Air Bout
Sustained Air Bout.description:
Keep fighting aloft for the whole length of an arena bout or an extended chase without losing altitude control as fatigue mounts.

With Endurance Conditioning the new element is duration: you tire, but you do not drop out of the airspace, which in an arena is a condition the judge would call. You still cannot hover indefinitely against a hard limit of stamina, a heavy load shortens everything, and the bout still ends by surrender, incapacitation, airspace conditions or stoppage. This is the body's own flight, with no rig or device in it.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Tight Air Engagement.name: Tight Air Engagement
Tight Air Engagement.description:
Fight in confined air, in corridors, hangars, stairwells and the gaps between structures, using short bursts of flight and contact with walls and fittings where open flight is impossible.

The scope grew from open sky to the spaces most Starian bouts avoid. It is still ordinary flight and your own body; the walls you touch are real and so are the fittings that give way. A space too narrow for your body is too narrow. One opponent at a time in such spaces, and any object in the air with you is a hazard to both. Bystanders in a corridor are not moved by it.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Live Demonstration.name: Live Demonstration
Live Demonstration.description:
Talk a willing learner through one specific task they have no practice in, step by step while it happens, so that they can make one guided attempt at basic competence under your direction.

The learner's attempt is real and theirs, made with your voice in their ear, and it stops being possible the moment you stop directing. One learner, one task, one attempt; it grants no lasting skill and cannot exceed what you yourself can do. A task that needs a tool or clearance the learner lacks is not made available by talk.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

Cohort Drill.name: Cohort Drill
Cohort Drill.description:
Train a willing group over days into one shared procedure, an evacuation, a search pattern, a handling routine, so that they carry it out together reliably later without you present.

The new outcome is a coordinated group action that exists after the training ends. It takes real time and repeated sessions, the participants must want it, and a procedure is not a skill: they can run the drill, not improvise beyond it. Roughly a squad or a class at a time. Nothing they learn exceeds what you know.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

Favour Call.name: Favour Call
Favour Call.description:
Call in a specific favour from an established contact to obtain an introduction, a door or a piece of information that is not for sale.

The contact must exist in play and the favour must be one they could plausibly grant; the price is the relationship, which is spent or strained by the call. One favour per call, and a contact who is frightened, absent or compromised cannot deliver. This does not create contacts or make anyone act against their own interest.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

Cross-House Introduction.name: Cross-House Introduction
Cross-House Introduction.description:
Arrange a meeting between parties who would not otherwise meet, across Houses, guilds or rival organisations, under your own name as the guarantor of good faith.

The new outcome is a table that did not exist. The guarantee is real: you carry the fallout if either side breaks faith, and both must be reachable through people you actually know. It secures the meeting, not its result, and does not bind anyone to attend a second time. Parties at open war are beyond it.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

Cuff and Carry.name: Cuff and Carry
Cuff and Carry.description:
Secure a subdued person with actual restraints, ties, cuffs or an improvised binding, and move them a distance without injuring them or letting them slip.

The restraints must be to hand; none are created. One person, already subdued, and the carry is at your actual strength over ground you can walk. A person who wakes or recovers fights the carry, and a rough carry over a long way is itself an injury to avoid.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

Clean Subdual.name: Clean Subdual
Clean Subdual.description:
Subdue one resisting person, armed at contact range or unarmed, with no injury beyond bruising, in a form a judge, a medic or a superior accepts as proportionate.

The narrator honours the outcome: the person is held and unhurt, and the method reads as restraint rather than assault. A person fully committed to killing may still defeat the attempt, and a weapon at range is not addressed. One person; it costs heavily in stamina and position, and it is not a hold that keeps itself.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

Operation Board.name: Operation Board
Operation Board.description:
Keep a running picture of a multi-part operation, its people, timings, supplies and communications, so that you notice the moment a piece is late, missing or reporting wrongly.

This depends on reports actually reaching you; a silent team is a gap you notice, not a location you know. It covers one operation at a time, and the picture is as good as its inputs. It does not command anyone or fix what it finds.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

Plan Re-Sequencing.name: Plan Re-Sequencing
Plan Re-Sequencing.description:
Re-sequence a failing operation in progress, reassigning tasks, timings and supplies from what is actually still available, so that it remains viable instead of collapsing.

The new outcome is a plan that survives contact. It works with the people and resources on hand, who must agree to their new parts; it is not command over strangers or a way of producing what was lost. One re-sequencing per crisis, and a plan with nothing left to re-sequence is over.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

Work Through Injury.name: Work Through Injury
Work Through Injury.description:
Complete a task needing fine control, aiming, treating a wound, operating a control, while injured, without the pain degrading the work.

This keeps the hands steady, not the body whole: a broken limb still does not work, bleeding still bleeds, and finishing the task may make the injury worse. One task while the injury lasts, at your actual skill, and it does not dull pain afterwards.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

Stand Through Shock.name: Stand Through Shock
Stand Through Shock.description:
Remain conscious, upright and coherent through a major injury that would drop another person, for long enough to finish what you are doing, withdraw or be treated.

The new outcome is minutes of function where there would be none. Blood loss, poison and a killing wound are not suspended; you fall when the body actually fails, and the collapse afterwards is real and total. It is not a return to fighting strength and it does not heal anything.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

Standard Sign-Off.name: Standard Sign-Off
Standard Sign-Off.description:
Inspect a piece of work or a piece of equipment in your own field and certify it to a professional standard that others in the trade and its clients accept as a sign-off.

The new outcome is that your word carries formal weight. It applies only within a trade you actually practise, only to work you have inspected in full, and a wrong sign-off is on your name. It does not fix what fails inspection.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

Reference Work.name: Reference Work
Reference Work.description:
Produce a piece of work in your trade that becomes a reference others measure against, an exemplar the trade recognises.

This takes the proper time, materials and tools of the trade; there is no shortcut in it. One piece, in one trade you practise, and its standing is earned in play as others see it. It does not make later work automatically as good.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

Own Wound Stabilization.name: Own Wound Stabilization
Own Wound Stabilization.description:
Treat your own injury under threat, stopping bleeding or splinting, and get back into action without waiting for someone else's hands.

Supplies must be on you; nothing is conjured. One injury, treated to stable rather than healed, and the treatment takes moments in which you are exposed. An injury you cannot reach or see stays untreated.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

Return to Action.name: Return to Action
Return to Action.description:
Recover from a knockdown, a winding or a stun and return to full action while others who took the same thing are still down.

The new outcome is speed of return, not immunity: injuries are not healed by it, and a second blow lands on the same body. It works once per knockdown and needs a moment of breath. Unconsciousness from a proper blow is not shortened by it.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

Stretch the Stores.name: Stretch the Stores
Stretch the Stores.description:
Ration a stated stock of supplies, food, water, cells, medical consumables, so that it lasts noticeably longer than its nominal count without harm to those depending on it.

The narrator honours the stretch as a real extension, not a doubling; it is care and sequencing, and it only works on stock you control and can account. It does not create supply, and when the stock is gone it is gone.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

Field Substitution.name: Field Substitution
Field Substitution.description:
Substitute an unavailable resource with something at hand, another fuel, a different part, a comparable medicine, an unfamiliar food, that actually serves the purpose.

The substitute must exist in the scene and be recognisable to you as workable; it does no better than the original and may do worse. One substitution per need, and a substitution that fails safely is the standard, not one that guesses.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

Unbaited Stance.name: Unbaited Stance
Unbaited Stance.description:
Remain outwardly unmoved by a deliberate provocation, an insult, a threat, a staged incident, designed to make you act, so that the provocateur gains no reaction to use.

The narrator honours it: you act only when you choose, not when they choose. It does not stop a physical attack and does not make the provocation harmless to others; it keeps your hands where you want them. One provocation at a time.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

Held Weapon.name: Held Weapon
Held Weapon.description:
Hold a weapon or a strike ready on a live target through a prolonged standoff without firing or striking early, and release only on your own decision.

The new outcome is a standoff that does not end by your nerves. Fatigue is real over a long hold, and a target who moves first is not stopped by your patience. It does not hold anyone else's hand; if others fire, they fire.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

Room Map.name: Room Map
Room Map.description:
In a gathering, identify who defers to whom, who is armed, who is afraid, and who is watching whom, from what is visible.

This reads what bodies and eyes show and nothing more; a room of trained faces gives less. It does not tell you why, does not reach through walls, and covers the room you are in at that moment.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

Tell Reading.name: Tell Reading
Tell Reading.description:
Detect that a person you are speaking with is concealing something or intends something other than what they say.

The new outcome is knowing that something is off, not what it is. Trained deceivers may pass, it is not mind reading and it does not reveal content. One person at a time, in conversation you can actually see.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

Measured Force.name: Measured Force
Measured Force.description:
Deliver a strike at exactly the intensity you chose, a warning tap, a stunning blow or a full strike, and land that and no more.

The narrator honours the chosen intensity; the target's actual fragility still decides the result. It does not make a strike land, and against armour or a much larger body a measured blow may do nothing at all.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

Single Blow Finish.name: Single Blow Finish
Single Blow Finish.description:
End an exchange with one committed strike at the exact moment an opponent's opening appears.

The new outcome is an ending, in an arena by stoppage or incapacitation. It needs an actual opening in one opponent; a failed strike leaves you fully extended. Not a killing technique and not repeatable in the same exchange.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

Joint Target.name: Joint Target
Joint Target.description:
Strike a specific joint or structural point to take one limb's function away for the exchange.

Armour, anatomy and a target that moves decide whether it works; it is a temporary loss of function, not a break. One limb, one strike, one opponent.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

Structural Strike.name: Structural Strike
Structural Strike.description:
Read the weak point of an object or construct, a drone's mount, a door's latch, a rig's strut, and strike it to break it.

The new target class is things rather than bodies. Hardened materials still need tools, the strike costs you the moment and possibly the hand, and it only works on a point you can actually reach and see.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

Field Bypass.name: Field Bypass
Field Bypass.description:
Bypass a failed component so that a machine runs in a degraded state until proper repair.

It is a bypass, not a fix: the machine runs worse and may fail again; parts to hand only. One component, one machine, and a bypass that would be unsafe is not made.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

Cold Rebuild.name: Cold Rebuild
Cold Rebuild.description:
Rebuild a machine into a working whole from salvaged parts of different machines.

The new outcome is a working machine where none existed; parts must exist and be compatible enough, and it takes proper time and tools. The result is as good as its worst part.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

District Shortcut.name: District Shortcut
District Shortcut.description:
Know a back way through a district, service passages, roofs, transit, that gets you across faster than the streets.

Only in districts you actually know; locked doors stay locked, and a passage that has changed since you learned it may not be there. One crossing at a time.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

Lose the Tail.name: Lose the Tail
Lose the Tail.description:
Shake a pursuer in the city by route choice, crowds and transit, so that they lose sight of you.

The new outcome is that a pursuer loses you rather than merely lags. It needs a district you know and a crowd or transit to use; a pursuer with a drone, a tracker or air support may keep contact regardless.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

Fault Catch.name: Fault Catch
Fault Catch.description:
Catch a flaw in a working, your own or another's, before it is invoked, so that it fails safe rather than misfires.

You must actually inspect it, and catching is not fixing. One working at a time; a flaw you cannot perceive from where you stand is not caught.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

Safe Abort.name: Safe Abort
Safe Abort.description:
Collapse an active working of your own, or one you can touch and read with its maker's consent, releasing its held Vitality without backlash.

The new outcome is an abort with no injury. Not a dispel of hostile workings, not a refund of what was already paid; only what is still held is released. One working, in contact.

[practiced advantage, not a new power sys]

Meshed Guard.name: Meshed Guard
Meshed Guard.description:
Mesh your guard with one consenting ally so that each of you covers the other's open side through an exchange.

The scope grew from a single guard to two, and it depends on the ally's actual cooperation and a word or signal between you; it is not a formation and does not make the ally competent. Two people, one shared front. A third person nearby is not included, and if the ally breaks away the guard is yours alone again.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Rehabilitation Care.name: Rehabilitation Care
Rehabilitation Care.description: Bring a body back after injury, strain or surgery: graded conditioning, prosthetic integration, protocols for overtrained and affinity-strained frames, the patience to hold a patient at less than they want. Slow by nature; it cannot regrow what is gone, and a patient who ignores the schedule undoes the work.

Crisis Logistics.name: Crisis Logistics
Crisis Logistics.description: Feed, house and supply people through a shortage or an emergency: ration, cache, stretch, stage, reroute, and know what runs out first. It allocates what exists; it does not create supply, and every stretched ration is a debt paid later in health or morale.

Information Brokerage.name: Information Brokerage
Information Brokerage.description: Keep an unwritten map of who owes whom, who knows what and who talks to whom, and spend it in fragments: the name that opens a door, the rumour that arrives a day early, the favour called in at the right hour. Every use spends trust or a source; a map not fed by fresh conversation goes stale in weeks, and it covers only the circles actually kept.

Confidential Custody.name: Confidential Custody
Confidential Custody.description: Keep what must be kept: sealed records, a client's business, a family's most dangerous knowledge, the name of a source. Refusal is polite, complete and repeatable under flattery, grief, drink and interrogation. It protects what the keeper knows, not what others can find elsewhere, and a keeper can be removed even if not opened.

Operations Dispatch.name: Operations Dispatch
Operations Dispatch.description: Run a station, depot, interchange or gate schedule: staffing, overflow, timetables, the contingency for the contingency. Authority extends to the operation's own staff and systems; it does not command outside services, and no plan survives a crisis the schedule never modelled.

Trade Negotiation.name: Trade Negotiation
Trade Negotiation.description: Negotiate terms under pressure: hold the number, trade obligation for obligation, rebuild a collapsed deal in real time, walk out at the right moment. Works with parties who need the deal; it cannot compel, and a settlement improvised at speed is one that gets re-read later.

Composure Under Pressure.name: Composure Under Pressure
Composure Under Pressure.description: Hold steady under scrutiny, insult, inquiry, fire or a long bad day: no visible crack, no baited temper, no early move. Composure hides the reaction, it does not remove it; it can be worn down over time, and the calm is not competence at whatever the pressure is about.

Crowd Reading.name: Crowd Reading
Crowd Reading.description: Read the temper and flow of a gathering: where the mood is turning, who is drunk, who is being cornered, where a push would become a crush. The read covers what the crowd shows, not what individuals plan, and it degrades in darkness, noise or when the reader is themselves the centre of attention.

Systems Engineering.name: Systems Engineering
Systems Engineering.description: Design, revise or reverse-engineer a system so that it survives production, substitution and years of use: layered redundancy, repairable parts, a failure that cannot repeat the same way twice. Works from real constraints and real materials; a design is a promise, not a built thing, and someone still has to build it, test it and pay for it.

Procedural Authority.name: Procedural Authority
Procedural Authority.description: Use an office's real power exactly: certify, grade, void, delay, refuse, refer upward, and make each act stick because it was done by the book. The authority is the office's, not the holder's; it stops at the office's boundary, it can be appealed, and it is worthless against anyone the office cannot reach.

Crew Leadership.name: Crew Leadership
Crew Leadership.description: Lead a crew, staff, line, class or gang so that it does the work when the leader is not looking: assign, correct, protect, take the blame upward and pass the credit down. Loyalty is earned by conduct and spent by it; it commands the people who have agreed to be led, and no more.

Structural Read.name: Structural Read
Structural Read.description: Judge a building, hull, span, frame or scaffold by eye, touch and sound: where the load runs, what is bearing more than it should, where a crack will go next. Gives a sound-or-not verdict and the likely failure point, not a schedule; hidden work behind finished surfaces stays hidden without opening it.

Records Administration.name: Records Administration
Records Administration.description: Keep an office's filings, compliance, schedules and case routing accurate enough to survive hostile audit: the right form, the right stamp, the right copy in the right drawer, the case sent to the desk that can act on it. It moves paper, not policy; it cannot make an authority rule a certain way, and it is only as fast as the office it serves.

Coalition Building.name: Coalition Building
Coalition Building.description: Assemble allies across houses, trades, districts and factions who would not sit together on their own: find the shared grievance, choreograph the meeting, hold the coalition through its first disappointment. Coalitions are rented, not owned; they hold only while the shared interest does, and every member is also talking to someone else.

Face and Name Recall.name: Face and Name Recall
Face and Name Recall.description: Keep name, trade, family and temperament attached to every face that passes regularly, and pick a stranger out of a familiar crowd by gait alone. Recall is for people actually met or watched; it does not extend to reputations, and a deliberate disguise or long absence can defeat it.

Client Handling.name: Client Handling
Client Handling.description: Receive, seat, feed and manage guests, passengers, patients and customers so that the difficult ones leave content and the dangerous ones leave early. It is courtesy with a purpose, not authority; it cannot eject anyone by itself, and it fails on a guest who wants the scene more than the service.

Contract Reading.name: Contract Reading
Contract Reading.description: Read and structure an agreement before it reaches official form: find the clause the parties will fight over next year, the obligation nobody priced, the term that means two things. Drafts, reconciles and witnesses; it does not compel signature, and it cannot make a bad bargain good, only visible.

Combat Instruction.name: Combat Instruction
Combat Instruction.description: Drill fighters: fundamentals, corrective sparring, timing, injury-aware programme design, and the eye to see which habit will fail under pressure years before an examination catches it. It builds competence, not courage; instruction is limited by the instructor's own school, and a student can be taught to a technique but not to want it.

Fighter Assessment.name: Fighter Assessment
Fighter Assessment.description: Read a fighter in a few exchanges or a few minutes of watching: the dropped shoulder, the flinch under heat, the school in the footwork, the tell before the committed strike. Turns into targeting in a bout and into a training note outside one. It reads technique and habit, not intent or hidden weapons, and a fighter deliberately showing a false style can mislead it for a round.

Pilotage.name: Pilotage
Pilotage.description: Fly or drive a loaded vehicle where the licensed and the cautious will not: rough-field landings, threaded reaches, extraction under bad conditions. Within the craft's rated limits and the pilot's fatigue; weather, damage and an unfamiliar hull raise the risk, and a hard landing is still a landing only if everyone walks away.

Clinic Triage.name: Clinic Triage
Clinic Triage.description: Sort and treat the injured by what will kill them first, with a clinic's tools: airway, haemorrhage, shock, burns, fractures, the surgery that cannot wait. Decisions are made in seconds and some are wrong; the method saves the most, not everyone, and it needs hands, light, water and supplies that a raid can take away.

Pattern Recognition.name: Pattern Recognition
Pattern Recognition.description: See the structure under noisy records, sightings or performances: the recurring interval, the anomaly that does not belong, the trend before the instruments confirm it. Produces a hypothesis with its confidence, never proof; it must be checked against the real case, and it is worst exactly when the analyst most wants the pattern to be there.

Cargo Rigging.name: Cargo Rigging
Cargo Rigging.description: Rig, hoist, stack and secure loads with rope, cable, crane and counterweight so that nothing shifts in transit or falls on anyone. Within the rated capacity of the gear and the honest weight of the load; an overloaded line is a hazard, not a technique, and rigging at height is done slowly or not at all.

Patient Reading.name: Patient Reading
Patient Reading.description: Read a body for what is wrong with it: strain, fever, concealed injury, overtraining, the bleed under an unbroken surface, the stress that will become a collapse. Gives a working diagnosis to act on, with what remains uncertain named; it is not treatment, and it cannot read what the patient hides from touch and sight.

Escort Positioning.name: Escort Positioning
Escort Positioning.description: Move with a protected person so that the threat has to come through the escort: exits chosen before entering, distance managed, the client's body never between the escort and the danger. It manages observed threats; an unseen shooter, a crowd crush or a client who bolts defeats it, and the escort is not the fighting solution, only the first one.

Institutional Memory.name: Institutional Memory
Institutional Memory.description: Recall how an office, house, academy or yard has actually done things: every exception granted, who ruled what, which procedure is real and which is decorative. Faster than the records and annotated with why. The memory is only as good as what the holder witnessed or was told, and it carries their loyalties with it.

Workshop Fabrication.name: Workshop Fabrication
Workshop Fabrication.description: Build, machine and assemble parts, fixtures and one-off tools in a workshop, including improvised fabrication from reclaimed stock when the proper part does not exist. Output is limited by tooling, stock and time; an improvised part is a stand-in with a shorter life, and precision work needs the bench, not the field.

Failure Forensics.name: Failure Forensics
Failure Forensics.description: Work back from a broken machine, burnt circuit, failed part or wrecked vehicle to the sequence that killed it, and separate wear from abuse from sabotage. Findings need the pieces in hand and time to compare them; a clean sabotage by a competent hand can read as fatigue, and the method names the cause, not the culprit.

Civic Administration.name: Civic Administration
Civic Administration.description: Run a public office, welfare system, market authority or district programme: budgets, policy, staff, the meeting where the decision actually gets made. Authority is what the office grants and nothing more; it moves slowly, leaves a record, and can be overruled by whoever funds it.

Material Assessment.name: Material Assessment
Material Assessment.description: Tell grade, origin and condition of stock by hand, eye and test: alloy from alloy, sound timber from rot, honest cloth from dressed cloth, the undocumented substitution in a finished part. Reports what the sample supports and states what would need a lab; it does not certify a whole lot from one piece.

Kitchen Craft.name: Kitchen Craft
Kitchen Craft.description: Feed people well from what the stores hold: plan, cook, preserve, stretch and correct, for one table or a camp. Bounded by ingredients, fuel and hands; it does not make spoiled stock safe, and cooking for a crowd is logistics before it is flavour.

Textile Craft.name: Textile Craft
Textile Craft.description: Cut, fit, dye, weave and repair cloth and leather for working bodies of every build, and make garments outlast their price. Limited by cloth, dye and time; it does not make armour of fabric, and colour and fit are only as true as the stock allows.

Trust Building.name: Trust Building
Trust Building.description: Turn strangers into sources and sources into allies by conduct: keep confidences, pay debts early, tell the truth at cost, show up. Trust is slow to build and instant to lose; it cannot be demanded, it does not transfer to a stranger vouching in the trusted one's name, and one visible betrayal spends all of it.

Caravan Driving.name: Caravan Driving
Caravan Driving.description: Drive a loaded vehicle or a hauler train through fords, switchbacks, bad weather and a caravan's worth of stops, and bring cargo and passengers in on schedule. Bounded by the vehicle, the load and the road; a failing rig, a washed-out ford or an ambush is the driver's problem before it is anyone else's, and speed is bought with wear.

Courier Work.name: Courier Work
Courier Work.description: Move messages, parcels and small cargo across a district or a route on time: know the handoffs, the transport that actually runs, the door that opens fastest on each street. Reliability is the product, not speed; a route never run is a guess, and a courier carries what fits in two hands.

Field Repair.name: Field Repair
Field Repair.description: Fix water, heat, doors, cookers, gear and machines with ordinary tools and whatever parts are in reach, and make the fix hold. Repairs stay within the tools and parts to hand: no fabrication of what is missing, no bypass of a safety that was doing its job, and a repair made in the field is a repair that needs a proper one later.

Legal Maneuvering.name: Legal Maneuvering
Legal Maneuvering.description: Use law, precedent and procedure as terrain: the filing that delays, the hearing that forces disclosure, the provision that looks small until it is stacked with five others. Effective only inside a jurisdiction that still honours its own rules; against a party willing to ignore the court it is paper. It takes time, often years, and it leaves a record.

People Reading.name: People Reading
People Reading.description: Hear what a speaker is not saying: rehearsed answers, hidden stress, the question they are steering away from, the lie built on a half-truth. Gives a confident read on sincerity and pressure, not the concealed fact itself. It fails against practised deceivers who believe their own story and against anyone the reader wants too badly to trust.

Teaching Craft.name: Teaching Craft
Teaching Craft.description: Bring a student from not knowing to doing: sequence the lesson, find the misunderstanding under the wrong answer, adjust to the learner in front of you, notice hunger and fear before the work explains them. It changes what the student can do, not what they choose to; and a teacher's praise, once cheapened, stops working.

Dispute Mediation.name: Dispute Mediation
Dispute Mediation.description: Sit between two parties who both think they are right and get to an agreement they will both keep: hear each fully, find the interest under the position, propose the split nobody loves and everyone signs. Needs both sides to prefer settlement to victory; it has no enforcement, and a party with an outside option walks.

Household Management.name: Household Management
Household Management.description: Run a compound, guest house or family home so that everyone is fed, placed and gently managed, on a budget that can be halved without guests noticing. It buys order, not safety: the household's defence is whoever it employs for that, and the work is invisible only until the person doing it stops.

Route Reading.name: Route Reading
Route Reading.description: Read ground, air, water and weather for the route that will hold: where the wind funnels, which corridor closes after rain, which lane the traffic will take, where a load will not fit. Reads conditions, not opposition, and reads only what the traveller can see or has travelled; a route never taken is a guess.

Interrogation Method.name: Interrogation Method
Interrogation Method.description: Get an account out of someone who would rather not give one: sequence questions, let silence work, cross-check against what is already known, notice the answer that was prepared. Produces an account with its contradictions marked, not the truth; it does not use force, and a subject who refuses to speak has refused.

Archive Search.name: Archive Search
Archive Search.description: Find the thing in the stacks: cross-reference catalogues, reconcile versions, restore a damaged page, and say which source supports which claim. Limited to archives the searcher can reach and read; sealed, missing or deliberately mis-shelved material stays lost, and the method reports gaps rather than filling them.

Crisis Coordination.name: Crisis Coordination
Crisis Coordination.description: Run an emergency: seals, evacuation, casualty flow, relay, who goes where and in what order, with or without formal authority. Command lasts as long as people are willing to be commanded and the picture is current; it cannot see through walls, and every minute of confusion at the start is paid for at the end.

Public Speaking.name: Public Speaking
Public Speaking.description: Hold a crowd with a voice: the toast, the argument, the lecture, the rally, the performance that makes a room listen. It moves a room's mood and attention, not its convictions overnight; hecklers, noise and a hostile venue cut it down, and a speech is remembered longer than the speaker would like.

Endurance Conditioning.name: Endurance Conditioning
Endurance Conditioning.description: Keep going: long shifts, long chases, long watches, pain and cold and bad sleep, without the work getting worse. It is stamina and tolerance, not immunity; the body still pays, later and with interest, and conditioning for one kind of strain does not transfer to another.

Cover Documentation.name: Cover Documentation
Cover Documentation.description: Make paper say what it needs to: a plausible manifest, a cover identity that survives a clerk, a record that ends where questions would start, evidence that is no longer there. Every artefact is a liability that outlives its use; it fools a check, not an investigation, and a professional comparison against the genuine article breaks it.

Pursuit Craft.name: Pursuit Craft
Pursuit Craft.description: Follow a person, a trail or a vehicle over ground and time: read the sign, predict the turn, close when they tire, keep the quarry from knowing. Limited by the pursuer's own stamina and by ground that takes no sign; a target who changes transport or has help waiting breaks the chase.

Checkpoint Procedure.name: Checkpoint Procedure
Checkpoint Procedure.description: Run a gate, desk or ring transfer by the book: scan the permit, match the face, confirm the work order, refuse the gap, log the refusal, call the next authority. Authority ends at the post; it is not gate command, not arrest power and not an interrogation licence. A perfect forgery passes it, and so does anyone the post's own rules exempt.

Counseling.name: Counseling
Counseling.description: Sit with the grieving, the frightened and the driven and help them act: take testimony without breaking the speaker, name the next step, hold hope at the size the facts allow. It is presence and method, not cure; it does not work on someone who wants an audience rather than a way through, and it costs the counsellor.

Cargo Assessment.name: Cargo Assessment
Cargo Assessment.description: Price, grade and weigh goods, cargo and salvage from manifest and inspection: what it is worth here, what it is worth three stops on, and whether the crate matches the paper. Estimates carry a stated margin and depend on market familiarity; an unfamiliar trade good or a sealed crate gets a range, not a number.

Discreet Inquiry.name: Discreet Inquiry
Discreet Inquiry.description: Find out without being seen to ask: which clerk to buy tea for, which ostler talks, how to triangulate a rumour against a manifest and a face. Produces leads and contradictions, never proof; it costs favours, time and sometimes a source, and a subject who learns of the inquiry closes every door it opened.

Close Combat.name: Close Combat
Close Combat.description: Fight at contact range with trained fundamentals: strikes, clinch, footwork, the plain doctrine of hurting the other person first and not stopping. Competent, not exceptional; it does not overcome a house-trained fighter, an affinity user at full expression, or a weapon it has no answer for, and it costs stamina fast.

Animal Handling.name: Animal Handling
Animal Handling.description: Settle, work and care for stock and working animals, including the ones that give others trouble. Calm and patience, not command; a panicked herd, an injured animal in pain or a predator is beyond it, and it does nothing for people.

Nonlethal Restraint.name: Nonlethal Restraint
Nonlethal Restraint.description: End a confrontation with holds, leverage and position rather than injury: warning, redirection, distance, then the hold. It controls one person at a time within their real resistance; a stronger, armed or affinity-backed opponent breaks it, and it is not a technique for the middle of a melee.

Formation Command.name: Formation Command
Formation Command.description: Direct armed units as one instrument: deploy, hold, deny ground, rotate the line, pull back before it breaks. Effective only over troops trained to the doctrine and within the communications actually available; a formation whose commander is down or cut off reverts to its own fallback, and the plan is worth what its scouts saw.

Salvage Work.name: Salvage Work
Salvage Work.description: Strip, sort and recover what is worth keeping from wreckage, ruins and waste streams, and know what is worth the risk of getting it out. Limited by what can be reached, carried and safely cut; unstable structures, live systems and contested ground are the usual reasons the good part stays where it is.

Threat Reading.name: Threat Reading
Threat Reading.description: Read a room, street or approach for the person who is about to become a problem: weight shifts, hand placement, eyes that check exits, tempers past their edge. Gives early warning and a likely first move, not a certain one; a trained infiltrator or a calm professional can pass the read. Works only on people actually in view and says nothing about what they carry that cannot be seen.

Forgery Detection.name: Forgery Detection
Forgery Detection.description: Compare a document, seal, mark or maker's hand against the genuine article and say whether it is what it claims to be. Detects altered pages, copied hands, restruck seals and substituted provenance; states plainly what could not be verified. It cannot name the forger and it does not work on an original the inspector has never seen an example of.

Verbatim Recall.name: Verbatim Recall
Verbatim Recall.description: Hold the exact words, figures or sequence of a document, conversation or count and reproduce them later without drift. Covers what was actually heard or seen with attention; it does not fill gaps, and fatigue, injury or a deliberately noisy room degrade the take.

Shop Stewardship.name: Shop Stewardship
Shop Stewardship.description: Keep a shop, stall, bar or small business solvent: stock what sells, price what does not, know the regulars, keep the books honest enough for the inspector and quiet enough for the family. It manages a business, not a market; it does not set prices beyond the door or make a bad location good.

Patrol Mapping.name: Patrol Mapping
Patrol Mapping.description: Know a watch as a timetable: when the rounds pass, where the sightlines break, which gate is lazy at shift change, how a breach would be run. Built from observation over days, not instinct; a rotation changed since the last look invalidates the map, and it says nothing about unseen guards.

Field Medicine.name: Field Medicine
Field Medicine.description: Stabilise a casualty where they fell: stop the bleed, splint, clean, dose, keep them warm and breathing until real care arrives. It is first response, not treatment; internal injury, deep burns and poisoning are beyond it, and every field measure is a bridge to a clinic, not a substitute.

Stealth and Concealment.name: Stealth and Concealment
Stealth and Concealment.description: Go unnoticed: dress and move as someone who belongs, slip a tail, cross a district without a record, use cover and timing instead of speed. Concealment is relative to the watcher; trained eyes, good light and checkpoints that count heads defeat it, and it ends the moment attention is drawn by anyone else.

Crowd Control.name: Crowd Control
Crowd Control.description: Separate, channel and hold a crowd or a bar floor: create distance, take the loud one aside, close the door before the push. Presence does most of it; force, when used, is the smallest that works. It holds a crowd that still recognises authority, not a riot, and one bad move turns it into the thing it was preventing.

Heavy Labor.name: Heavy Labor
Heavy Labor.description: Carry, haul, dig and lift for a full shift and be useful at the end of it: yard work, farm work, stable work, general labour. Within the body's real capacity, with rest; it is endurance, not strength beyond the frame, and injury or bad footing ends it.

De-escalation.name: De-escalation
De-escalation.description: Take the heat out of a confrontation before contact: name what each side is afraid of, give the loud one a way to stop that is not losing, separate, delay, feed. It works on people who still want a way out; it does nothing against a planned attack, and it buys minutes, not resolution.

Courier Running.name: Courier Running
Courier Running.description: Run a district or a route fast and arrive able to speak: pacing, knowing the cut-throughs, the hour when the market thins. Speed is bounded by legs and load; it is not pursuit-proof, and a runner carrying more than a satchel is a walker.

Rooftop Running.name: Rooftop Running
Rooftop Running.description: Move across a city vertically: roofs, walls, gutters, crawlspaces, the gap that is shorter than it looks. Fast on ground the runner knows and dangerous on ground they do not; wet stone, a loose tile or a locked hatch ends the run, and it carries nothing heavier than the runner.

Forge Handling.name: Forge Handling
Forge Handling.description: Work hot metal and edged steel: forge, temper, balance, sharpen, fit a blade or harness to the body that will use it. Quality is bounded by stock, fuel and time; a blade tuned to one fighter is tuned wrong for another, and no edge survives misuse the smith did not see.

Fine Craftwork.name: Fine Craftwork
Fine Craftwork.description: Do precise handwork: glass, lenses, seals, instruments, calligraphy, inlay, conservation of fragile pieces. The work needs steady hands, good light and time; it cannot be hurried without loss, and a piece that fails in the making is stock spent.

Defensive Fundamentals.name: Defensive Fundamentals
Defensive Fundamentals.description: Trained, unglamorous defence: guard up, feet under, meet or redirect what can be seen, protect the head and the hands, disengage when the ground stops being yours. It keeps an ordinary person alive against an ordinary attacker; it does not win fights, and it fails against numbers, weapons the guard was not trained for, or an opponent who is simply better.

Counter Work.name: Counter Work
Counter Work.description: Win by the other fighter's expenditure: break their rhythm, bait the committed strike, redirect what arrives, make the chase a tax that compounds. Needs an opponent who attacks; against patience it is a stalemate, against numbers it is a delay, and it depends on the counter-fighter's own stamina lasting longer than the aggressor's.

Historical Custodianship.name: Historical Custodianship
Historical Custodianship.description: Carry a family's, town's or house's unwritten history: the raids, the debts, the shape of a conflict before the current generation was born, the names that must not be forgotten. Sharing is itself a decision and the custodian chooses when. It is memory and testimony, not a document; it can be wrong, and it dies with the keeper unless passed on.

Drone Link.name: Drone Link
Drone Link.description: Direct, read and re-task drone units within the authority actually granted: assign formation, route, watch or carry work, and understand unexpected unit behaviour as information before reset. Units answer to their governing authority, not the operator; a link can be denied, jammed or superseded, and no drone does what its class was not built to do.

Market Trading.name: Market Trading
Market Trading.description: Buy and sell at the price the moment supports: read the other side's floor, hold silence past it, trade favour for margin, walk away when the number is wrong. Works within a real market and a real budget; it cannot conjure demand, and a counterpart who does not need the deal cannot be moved by it.

Blade Work.name: Blade Work
Blade Work.description: Fight with an edged weapon as a trained practitioner: measure, guard, cut, thrust, recovery, and the discipline to keep the edge where it belongs. Competent within one school; it is not mastery of every blade, it loses reach to a polearm and initiative to a firearm, and a blade is only as good as the smith who kept it.

Pharmacological Craft.name: Pharmacological Craft
Pharmacological Craft.description: Compound, dose and test remedies, sedatives, stimulants and antidotes from stock and field plants, and know what each does to a two-hearted body under load. Within known ingredients and documented doses; an unfamiliar plant is an experiment, and a dose set for one physiology can poison another.

River Pilotage.name: River Pilotage
River Pilotage.description: Handle a boat or barge on moving water: read the current, thread a crowded reach, land where the bank allows, recover someone from the river. Bounded by the vessel, the load and the water; a flood, a night crossing or a hull the pilot does not know is a different river.

Genesis Breaker.name: Genesis Breaker
Genesis Breaker.description:
Condense crimson energy into a single focused point and drive it through an opponent's guard, shield or armor, breaking the defense rather than the body behind it.

Ark Genesis developed it outside the House Genesis standard; it is learned only near the top of both the crimson affinity and Genesis combat ladders. Gathering the point takes a committed strike, a read opponent can slip it, and each strike breaks one defense.

Crimson Ascension.name: Crimson Ascension
Crimson Ascension.description:
Release the full might of your crimson energy and become living crimson energy, nearly tripling speed and combat capability while it lasts. It drains energy and affinity rapidly; when it ends, by choice or by running dry, the body reverts to flesh with its crimson reserves spent, and anything further is Starian strength and will alone.

Ark Genesis's signature, learned only at the very top of both the crimson affinity and Genesis combat ladders.

High Approach.name: High Approach
High Approach.description: Take the higher line before an opponent does, arriving above them with room to choose the next move. It needs actual open sky above you; a ceiling, a storm or a crowded lane takes it away. Starting trained action only. Resolve against the actual scene and relevant skills; no bonus stacking, new power, item or automatic success.

Descent Strike.name: Descent Strike
Descent Strike.description:
Drop from altitude onto one opponent below with the whole height of the fall behind a single strike. The descent is seen coming by anyone watching the sky, a missed strike leaves you low and slow, and it needs real height to be worth anything.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Wake Pressure.name: Wake Pressure
Wake Pressure.description:
Pass close enough that your wake unsettles one flier's line and forces them to correct. It moves them, not harms them; a heavy or grounded opponent barely feels it.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Angle Denial.name: Angle Denial
Angle Denial.description:
Hold the airspace around one opponent so that every approach they try arrives at a worse angle than the last. It works in open sky against one flier; a second opponent or a ground threat breaks it.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Exhaustion Circuit.name: Exhaustion Circuit
Exhaustion Circuit.description:
Keep one airborne opponent climbing, turning and recovering, never letting them settle, until they tire before you do. It lasts only as long as your own flight endurance, and a patient opponent who lands refuses it.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Open Sky Dominion.name: Open Sky Dominion
Open Sky Dominion.description:
Own a stretch of open sky against several fliers at once, reading every approach and taking each opponent at the angle that favours you. This is the Aevon tradition at its height and may be named as such. It ends where the open sky ends; bring it to ground and it is gone.

[trained action only; resolve against the actual scene]

Old Form Root.name: Old Form Root
Old Form Root.description: Set a stance that resists being pushed, pulled or rushed off the spot you chose. Starting trained action only. Resolve against the actual scene and relevant skills; no bonus stacking, new power, item or automatic success.

Old Form Exchange.name: Old Form Exchange
Old Form Exchange.description:
